HROS: Human Resource Operating Standards

i.

Foreword

Foreword (Option 1)

It gives me great pleasure to introduce the JSW Motors HR Operations Manual.

As a young brand, we have a unique opportunity to build the right culture, standards and ways of working from the very beginning. The choices we make today will shape the experience of our employees, dealer partners and customers for years to come.

At JSW Motors, we believe that great customer experiences are created by engaged, capable and confident people. When our employees feel supported, developed and valued, they bring that same commitment to every customer interaction.

This manual provides a strong framework for managing the employee lifecycle, from hiring and onboarding to development, performance, rewards and separation. It is designed to help our dealer partners build consistent people practices while ensuring a positive employee experience across the network.

This guide serves as a recommended standard, not a mandate. Our dealer partners remain the employer of record and retain full responsibility for employment decisions and legal compliance. Where stronger practices already exist, we encourage partners to continue and build upon them.

As we grow together, our success will be defined not only by the vehicles we sell, but by the trust we earn from our employees, partners and customers. We look forward to building a world-class dealer network founded on strong people practices and shared success.

Together, let's create a workplace and a customer experience that sets new standards for the industry.

[Name]
[Designation]
JSW Motors

Foreword (Option 2)

When I think about what will make JSW Motors successful, I don't think about market share or sales targets first. I think about people.

Every great business is built on a simple truth: take care of your people and they will take care of everything else. It's not a strategy or a mantra—it's just how things work when you pay attention.

The employees walking into our dealerships each morning are carrying more than just their job responsibilities. They're carrying their aspirations, their families' hopes, their desire to be part of something worthwhile. How we respond to that - how we train them, support them when things get difficult, recognize their contributions, help them grow—that's the foundation we're building on.

This manual isn't about rules and procedures. It's about building the kind of workplace where people can do their best work. Where a young service advisor can see a path forward. Where a receptionist feels their role matters. Where a technician can take pride in their craft. Where a sales consultant feels he is bringing life to a customer’s dream of buying a car.

We're starting with a clean slate in JSW Motors and that's both exciting and humbling. We are standing at a point wherein we have a chance to get it right from day one - to create an environment where people want to come to work, where they feel valued and where they can see their future.

This guide gives our dealer partners the tools to build that foundation. The rest - the sales, the growth, the customer loyalty - will follow naturally.

At the end of the day, we're not really in the automobile business. We're in the people business. The cars are just what brings us together.

Foreword (Option 3)

We're bringing something special to India with JSW Motors - a world-class product with a distinctly Indian heart. Everything about this brand has been crafted to meet global standards while staying true to what Indian customers value and deserve.

That same philosophy needs to come alive in how we build our teams. We have an incredible opportunity here: to create a dealer network where every employee embodies this blend of international excellence and local understanding. Where professionalism meets warmth. Where efficiency meets genuine care.

The market we're entering isn't just competitive - it's full of possibility. Customers today are more discerning, more informed and more willing to embrace brands that truly understand them. That's our opening. And the people in our dealerships are the ones who will turn that opportunity into reality.

Every employee - from the sales consultant to the service technician to the person answering phones - is carrying our brand reputation in their hands. They are the ones who will either build trust. They are the ones who turn a transaction into a relationship. They are the ones who create the experiences that customers remember.

This manual is designed to help our dealer partners create the conditions for those employees to succeed. Because when we invest in our people - when we give them proper training, clear expectations, growth opportunities and genuine support - they don't just work for us. They become advocates for our customers.

An employee who feels valued doesn't just show up for a pay check. They go the extra mile. They solve problems creatively. They make customers feel important because they know what that feels like themselves.

As we build the JSW Motors network across India, let's be clear about what we're really building: a community of professionals who are equipped, empowered and enthusiastic about creating exceptional customer experiences. That's the competitive advantage no one can copy.

Our people are the light that guides customers to us and keeps them with us. Let's make sure that light shines bright.

iii.

How to Read the Manual

HR Systems at a Glance

Essential HR Requirements for Every Dealership

Attracting, retaining and engaging the right people is what truly sets a dealership apart.

People & Leadership

  • Structured training for managers to conduct fair and effective appraisals
  • Clearly defined daily objectives and KPIs for every manager
  • Managers take ownership of employee engagement within their teams
  • Open and effective communication across all levels
  • A trained HR professional to build, implement and sustain HR systems
  • Senior leadership commitment to career and succession planning

Systems & Processes

  • Structured, institutionalised manpower planning
  • Clear standards for internal role movement and promotion
  • Standardised induction for every new joiner
  • A Performance Management System that covers every employee
  • Compensation benchmarked against the industry
  • A transparent incentive system that rewards performance fairly
  • An automated HR Management Information System (MIS) for timely reporting

Culture

  • Professional, process-driven decision-making
  • A sustainable, people-centric performance culture

Key HR Guidelines for Dealers

The HR guidelines in this manual are grouped into three levels, so every dealership can see where it stands today and what it should work towards:

1

Basic

The minimum standards that every JSW Motors dealership must follow.

  1. Manpower planning & talent acquisition
  2. Employee
  3. Compensation & Rewards management
2

Advance

Guidelines that help the dealership build a sustainable, employee-centric organisation.

  1. Performance management System
  2. Training & development
  3. Career planning
  4. Employee engagement
3

Leader

Best practices followed by exemplary dealerships that serve as role models across the network. These practices help build an engaged workforce through strong leadership and effective communication.

  1. Succession planning
  2. Communication
  3. Leadership developments

CHAPTER 1

Dealership Organisation Structure

"To win the marketplace, you must first win the workplace."
Objective:
  • To build an organisational structure which effectively utilises lean business resources and efficiently achieves company objectives
  • Provide dealer partners with an industry benchmarked organisation structure that is optimised as per outlet category
Benefit to Dealer:
  • Right-sized team helps deliver optimum results with better profitability
Benefit to Customer:
  • Faster and seamless customer journey
  • Consistent customer experience
  • Transparent communication

Principles

A robust organizational structure provides stability to the dealership operations through:

Role Clarity:

  • Responsibilities are defined
  • Employees take accountability as per their roles

Efficient Decision Making:

  • Correct hierarchy and decision tree
  • Communication flow via correct channels

Enhanced Collaboration:

  • Effective delegation
  • Clear functional and operational reporting

Resource Optimization:

  • Right person - right job
  • Higher productivity due to well-defined roles & responsibilities

    This chapter covers all roles required in the After sales function of a JSW Motors dealership. Select any role from the list to view its full profile - department, reporting line, education and experience benchmarks, key responsibilities, KPIs and competencies.

    General Manager - Service

    DepartmentAfter sales
    Reporting toBusiness Head/CEO
    Role ImpactDealership Performance, Customer Experience & Team Leadership

    Position Overview

    The General Manager – Service is responsible for leading the dealership’s overall Aftersales operations, including Service, Parts, Bodyshop, and Customer Retention. The role drives the Aftersales business plan, profitability, KPI achievement, and customer satisfaction while ensuring operational excellence across all departments.

    The role is also responsible for ensuring adequate manpower, workshop infrastructure, tools, equipment, and compliance with OEM standards and manufacturer requirements, including EV/PHEV service readiness.

    1. Education

    Graduate in Automobile/Mechanical Engineering or related discipline; MBA preferred.15+ years in automotive service/after-sales, with 5+ years in a leadership role.Relevant OEM certifications in service management or dealership operations are an advantage.

    2. Experience

    16–18 years of progressive experience in automotive dealership Aftersales operations, with at least 5–7 years in a department-head or business-head capacity.Demonstrated track record of managing P&L for service, parts, and body shop.Exposure to EV/PHEV service operations, infrastructure planning is highly desirable.

    3. Key Responsibilities

    • Formulate and execute the annual and monthly Aftersales business plan, aligned with JSW and dealership growth objectives.
    • Set department-wise targets (service throughput, parts revenue, body shop revenue, VAS penetration) and conduct regular performance reviews.
    • Own the Aftersales P&L — driving revenue growth, controlling costs, and improving overall profitability and Service absorption.
    • Plan manpower, budgets, tools and infrastructure to support current operations and future business scale-up, including EV/PHEV readiness.
    • Understand Spare Parts operations and monitor at a high level various spare parts inventory levels, availability, ageing and carrying costs in coordination with the Parts Manager.
    • Review and coach department heads (Service Manager, Parts Manager, Body Shop Manager, CRM) on performance against team KPIs.
    • Champion the customer experience agenda — monitoring CSI/NPS trends.
    • Personally review w.r.t. ensuring timely closure and root-cause correction. Also, resolve highly escalated customer complaints
    • Ensure the workshop maintains JSW-mandated EV/PHEV tools, high-voltage safety equipment, and certified technician coverage.
    • Drive cross-functional coordination with Sales to ensure a seamless ownership handover and customer experience.
    • Lead recruitment, training and succession planning for the Aftersales leadership pipeline.
    • Represent the Aftersales function in management reviews, OEM audits, and business planning meetings.

    4. Key Performance Indicators (KPIs)

    Business Performance
    • After sales revenue and profitability (Service, Parts and Bodyshop)
    • Service Absorption Ratio
    • Gross Profit Contribution
    • Revenue per Available Bay
    • Parts Inventory Turnover ratio
    • Parts fill rate/first-pick ratio
    • Service Capacity Utilization
    Customer Experience
    • Customer Satisfaction Index (CSI) / Net Promoter Score (NPS)
    • Complaint resolution turnaround time
    • Customer Retention Rate
    • Service Turnaround Time (TAT)
    • Fixed Right First Time Rate
    People & Governance
    • Department-head performance and target achievement
    • Manpower attrition rate
    • JSW audit compliance score

    5. Key Competencies

    OEM Training ComplianceStrategic business vision, planning and P&L managementStrong functional expertise in Aftersales/dealership service operationsCustomer-centric decision-makingCross-functional leadership and stakeholder managementTeam development, mentorship, coaching, and motivation.Analytical and data-driven problem-solvingUnderstanding of EV/PHEV, safety and infrastructure requirementsInventory and cost control disciplineBudgeting, financial acumen and negotiation skillsOEM standards Audit Score

    Service Manager

    DepartmentAfter Sales
    Reporting toGeneral Manager – Aftersales/ Dealer Principal
    Role ImpactService Revenue, Workshop Performance, Repair Quality and Customer Satisfaction

    Position Overview

    The Service Manager is responsible for managing dealership service and workshop operations, driving business performance, productivity, repair quality, and customer satisfaction. The role ensures compliance with OEM processes, quality, safety, and 5S standards while managing team performance, customer escalations, and EV/PHEV service readiness through trained manpower, appropriate tools, equipment, and safety practices

    1. Education

    Graduate in Mechanical Engineering, Automobile Engineering, or related discipline preferred.

    2. Experience

    6-10 years of experience in automotive aftersales operations, including workshop management, with 2+ years in a supervisory/managerial role.Strong knowledge of OEM service processes and hands-on experience in utilizing Dealer Management Systems (DMS) for operational monitoring and performance management.Experience in managing end-to-end dealer service operations, including workshop productivity, customer satisfaction, revenue, profitability, warranty compliance, service quality, and customer concern resolution.Proven ability to coordinate effectively with OEM, Parts Department, and dealership leadership to drive operational excellence and business performance.

    3. Key Responsibilities

    A. Service Business and Workshop Performance
    • Plan, monitor, and review service revenue, target achievement, customer retention, and workshop performance requirements.
    • Support General Manager in the preparation and management of service budgets, operating costs, workshop resources, and manpower requirements.
    • Review workshop capacity, job allocation, technician productivity, and resource utilization to support efficient daily operations with Workshop controller.
    • Monitor pending vehicles, repair progress, promised delivery commitments, and vehicle ; drive timely action on delays.
    • Review service performance and take corrective action where workshop output, productivity, quality, or customer experience requires improvement.
    B. Daily Workshop Operations and Repair Quality
    • Supervise day-to-day workshop operations to ensure jobs are monitored & completed within committed timelines
    • Monitor repeat repairs, rework, and customer feedback to identify recurring concerns and initiate root-cause-based corrective actions.
    • Ensure consistency of workshop processes, safety requirements, 5S practices, and brand standards.
    • Coordinate with the Parts team so that timely parts availability for vehicle repairs is ensured, and repair delays attributable to parts requirements are minimized.
    C. Customer Experience and Complaint Resolution
    • Monitor customer experience indicators, including CSI/NPS, and complaints.
    • Review and resolve escalated customer concerns in coordination with the CRM function and service teams.
    • Participate in customer discussions on concern resolution, if required, to provide assurance on closure actions.
    • Define and monitor counter measures for resolved customer cases, in coordination with the whole team members, to prevent recurrence.
    D. Team Leadership and Capability Development
    • Review team performance, identify operational and capability gaps, and arrange relevant interventions on Man, Machine, Methods as per RCA.
    • Support manpower forecasting, team retention, and deployment planning for service operations.
    • Build a culture of accountability, customer focus, quality, safety, and process adherence within the service team.
    • Support the workshop’s EV/PHEV service readiness through training, tools, safety precautions, and adherence to required operating practices.
    E. Governance and Cross-functional Coordination
    • Ensure compliance with dealership service processes, workshop safety requirements, 5S and brand standards.
    • Participate in warranty-claim approval processes where required under the Aftersales SOP.
    • Coordinate with relevant functions—including Parts, CRM, and workshop teams—to support timely repair completion and customer communication.
    • Review operational issues and ensure that actions, responsibilities, and closure status are appropriately tracked.

    4. Key Performance Indicators (KPIs)

    Business Performance
    • Service revenue and target achievement
    • Service operating-cost control
    • Customer retention performance
    Workshop Operations
    • Manpower productivity
    • Workshop capacity utilization
    • Vehicle TAT and on-time delivery
    • Same Day Delivery & Pending-vehicle status and ageing
    Customer Experience
    • Customer Satisfaction Index (CSI) / Net Promoter Score (NPS)
    • Repeat repair and rework percentage
    • Customer complaint-resolution status and TAT (CC/1000)
    People & Process
    • Root-cause analysis and corrective-action closure for recurring concerns
    • After Sales Brand standards audit performance scores
    • Workshop Skill mix & training completion
    • Team management skills

    5. Key Competencies

    Aftersales and workshop-operations knowledgeService-business planning and cost controlWorkshop productivity, capacity, and resource planningRepair-quality and process managementCustomer handling, complaint resolution, and customer-recovery mind-setTeam leadership, mentorship, motivation, coaching, and performance managementCommunication and cross-functional coordinationProblem-solving, root-cause analysis, and decision-makingSafety, 5S, and process-compliance orientationUnderstanding of EV/PHEV service and workshop-safety requirementsBrand-value orientationUnderstanding of Parts /inventory control processPending-job management

    EDP (Electronic Data Processing Executive)

    DepartmentAfter Sales – IT & Systems (EDP)
    Reporting toService Manager
    Role ImpactSystem availability; System Uptime; Secure Access Reporting Accuracy & DMS Operations

    Position Overview

    The EDP (Electronic Data Processing) Executive is responsible for managing dealership management systems (DMS), supporting IT hardware, and generating operational reports as per dealership standards. The role ensures system uptime, data accuracy, timely reporting, and smooth digital operations across after-sales.

    1. Education

    Diploma or Degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, BCA, B.Sc. (IT) or a related field.Training in DMS administration, Excel expertise, network support, and data security is desirable.

    2. Experience

    1 to 3 years of experience as an EDP Executive, IT Support Assistant, or Data Processing Executive in an automotive dealership or commercial enterprise.Experience in DMS administration and computer network troubleshooting is preferred.

    3. Key Responsibilities

    • Maintain and administer the Dealer Management System (DMS), and smooth daily system operations.
    • Create, modify, or deactivate user access against authorized requests, maintaining accurate permission and access-change records.
    • Provide first-level support for workshop computers, printers, LAN/Wi-Fi connectivity, and cashier billing terminals. Ensure workshop diagnostic scan tool laptops, and software interfaces have up-to-date OEM patches and stable connectivity.
    • Coordinate unresolved faults with the OEM IT helpdesk, DMS vendor, or designated IT support provider.
    • Maintain regular data backups of dealership systems and safeguard customer and operational data confidentiality in compliance with company policy.
    • Coordinate with OEM IT helpdesk and DMS software vendors to resolve software bugs, system crashes, or data sync errors.

    4. Key Performance Indicators (KPIs)

    System & Hardware Uptime
    • 100% uptime for billing stations, DMS terminals, and workshop diagnostic laptops

    5. Key Competencies

    Proficiency in Dealer Management Systems (DMS) and OEM portalsAdvanced Excel skills (data compilation, formulas, pivot tables, and dashboards)Basic IT hardware, printer, LAN/Wi-Fi, and software troubleshootingHigh attention to data accuracy, consistency, and record managementGood coordination skills with service managers, warranty staff, and software vendorsAbility to manage user access, master data, system records, and issue logs with accuracyKnowledge of basic data validation, report logic, filter selection, date controls, and variance checkingAbility to identify and escalate DMS, network, hardware, printer, POS, or diagnostic connectivity concernsStrong data confidentiality, password discipline, backup awareness, and document control habitsCalm, reliable, and service focused approach during system outages, billing disruption, and reporting deadlines

    Workshop Controller

    DepartmentWorkshop
    Reporting toService Manager
    Role ImpactWorkshop Productivity, Vehicle Load Management, Repair Quality, On-Time Delivery, EV/PHEV Safety and Customer Satisfaction

    Position Overview

    The Workshop Controller manages the daily flow of vehicles, repair work, workshop capacity, and delivery commitments across the workshop. The role is responsible for ensuring that jobs are planned, allocated, monitored, and progressed in a controlled manner based on technician capability, bay availability, job complexity, parts availability, safety requirements, and promised delivery timelines.

    The role maintains visibility of every active vehicle through defined repair stages—from inspection and diagnosis through repair, quality inspection, washing, and delivery readiness. The Workshop Controller identifies delivery risks early, coordinates recovery actions with relevant teams, supports quality and first-time-right performance, and escalates technical, safety, warranty, parts, and capacity constraints through the appropriate channels.

    1. Education

    ITI or Diploma in Automobile Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or related technical discipline.OEM training/certification in workshop operations, job control, quality processes/Lean management, Kaizen, Workshop-management systems, EV/PHEV workshop safety is desirable.

    2. Experience

    8+ years of experience as a Workshop Controller in an authorized automotive workshop.Experience in workshop job planning, technician and bay allocation, repair-progress monitoring, capacity management, quality follow-up, and delivery-risk management.Exposure to EV/PHEV repair planning, high-voltage work controls, technical escalations, software/programming requirements, charging concerns, and complex diagnostic-case management is preferred.

    3. Key Responsibilities

    A. Workshop Load Planning and Daily Control
    • Conduct a daily workshop-control review covering workshop load, carry-over vehicles, breakdown cases, technician attendance and availability, bay status, parts availability constraints, diagnostic escalations, quality rework, and delivery-risk cases.
    • Plan and monitor the movement of vehicles through all defined repair stages from Interactive Reception to Delivery readiness using available systems.
    • Maintain visibility of time taken, job status, hold reasons, pending actions, technician assignment, and promised delivery commitments at each repair stage.
    • Use the workshop-control board, or digital dashboard to maintain current workshop status.
    • Review workshop load against available bays, technician capacity, repair complexity, and expected job duration to support practical daily planning.
    • Identify carry-over vehicles and create or coordinate appropriate recovery actions to reduce avoidable backlog.
    B. Job Allocation and Repair Sequencing
    • Allocate work based on technician skill matrix, repair complexity, job priority, required tools, diagnostic or programming requirements, bay constraints, and safety risk.
    • Coordinate repair sequencing to minimize wastages due to unnecessary vehicle movement, duplicate dismantling, idle time, bay congestion, and avoidable waiting between repair stages.
    • Confirm that relevant parts, tools, technical information, supporting personnel, and workspace are available before the next repair operation begins.
    • Review job-card and repair-order details before allocation to ensure work requirements, customer concerns, and repair dependencies are understood.
    • Support accurate job status, allocation, and time-recording discipline in the DMS.
    C. Repair Progress, Delay Prevention and Delivery Commitment
    • Track repair progress against committed delivery time and identify at-risk jobs at an early stage.
    • Monitor risks such as pending diagnosis, part back-order, delayed approval, additional repairs, technician absence, programming or software-download time, equipment constraints, and other unforeseen dependencies.
    • Initiate corrective and recovery actions to prevent delays to the committed delivery time and communicate a revised timeline when operational constraints are confirmed.
    • Monitor Carry over vehicles by repair stage and follow up on vehicles that are pending diagnosis, approval, parts, repair, quality check, or delivery readiness.
    • Review daily planned output against actual output and highlight backlog, productivity, capacity, or delivery-performance gaps to the Service Manager.
    D. Technical Escalation, Warranty and Campaign Coordination
    • Review diagnostic findings, technician comments, additional work requirements, and job-completion status before the vehicle proceeds for quality inspection and subsequent delivery stages.
    • Coordinate handover of complex technical cases to the Diagnostic Expert, Electrical Expert, or JSW Technical Support, where these roles or channels are available.
    • Ensure that case summaries, diagnostic trouble codes, test results, repair history, photographs, technician observations, and work already performed are available for technical escalation.
    • Identify warranty-related repairs at an early stage and coordinate the availability of relevant repair documentation, causal-part details, diagnostic evidence, approvals, failed-part requirements, and technician comments for the Warranty Specialist.
    • Check for part availability for any technical campaign, recall, and service-action applicability at time of appointment/floor intake.
    E. Parts, Tools and Equipment Readiness
    • Coordinate with the Parts Manager or Parts team to monitor critical parts, special-order parts, VOR parts, campaign parts, battery/high-voltage-related parts.
    • Use expected parts-arrival information to revise the repair plan and support accurate delivery commitments.
    • Monitor the availability and serviceability of workshop tools and equipment required for scheduled work and escalate equipment unavailability, calibration and maintenance requirements, or system-connectivity issues that may affect repair quality, productivity, or vehicle delivery.
    F. Quality, Rework and Continuous Improvement
    • Coordinate repair-progress review with relevant workshop personnel to support completion of work before quality inspection.
    • Monitor internal rework, repeat repairs, delayed deliveries, idle time, bay blockage, and quality failures.
    • Identify recurring operational or quality issues, conduct or support root-cause analysis, and follow up on corrective actions through closure.
    • Ensure vehicles are sent for quality inspection only after repair completion and applicable repair-order updates.
    • Support compliance with required quality inspection, functional validation, road-test, washing, and delivery-readiness stages.
    • Coordinate with quality Inspector to share quality, repeat-repair, rework, and process-discipline trends with the Service Manager and relevant workshop teams.
    G. EV/PHEV Work Control and Workshop Safety
    • For EV/PHEV work, confirm that the job is assigned to an appropriately trained and authorized technician.
    • Confirm the required HV work status, personal protective equipment, safety equipment, controlled work area, tool availability, battery or charging considerations, and technical support route before repair work begins.
    • Immediately stop or escalate work where there is a potential safety concern, unclear repair method, suspected high-voltage or battery damage, missing safety controls, improper tool use, or activity outside the technician’s authorization.
    • Maintain awareness of EV/PHEV repair dependencies and coordinate appropriate escalation rather than independently authorizing technical or high-voltage work outside the role of authority.
    • Promote safe vehicle movement, key control, vehicle protection, workshop-floor discipline, cleanliness, and compliance with applicable safety and 5S requirements.
    H. Team Support, Training and Reporting
    • Coach technicians on proper time recording, repair-order discipline, job-status updates, repair-quality expectations, escalation practice, safe-work practices, and follow-through on assigned repair plans.
    • Communicate new technical or service bulletins and relevant process requirements to the workshop team, where assigned.
    • Identify skill gaps, training needs, and capability-development requirements for technicians, Diagnostic Experts, and Electrical Experts, and raise them with the Service Manager.
    • Provide concise daily and weekly operational reporting to the Service Manager on workshop load, output, productivity, efficiency, turnaround time, delivery performance, carry-over, ageing, repeat jobs, quality, safety, potential escalations, capacity constraints, and recovery actions.
    • Maintain a professional workshop environment consistent with approved dealership, OEM, and brand-process requirements.

    4. Key Performance Indicators (KPIs)

    Workshop Operations and Capacity Management
    • Technician productivity, efficiency, Utilization
    • Bay utilization and bay productivity
    • Daily planned output versus actual workshop output
    • Carry-over Ratio
    • Vehicle turnaround time (TAT)
    • On-time delivery performance
    Quality and Process Control
    • Repeat repair and internal rework rate
    • First-time-right / fix-right-first-time performance
    • Compliance with technician skill-matrix and job-allocation controls
    • Completion of quality inspection and required post-repair verification
    • Average Diagnosis resolution time
    • Technical Escalation: Number of issues resolved without OEM escalation.

    Diagnostic Expert (DE)

    DepartmentAfter Sales
    Reporting toWorkshop Controller
    Role ImpactDiagnostic Accuracy, Fix-Right-First-Time, High-Voltage Safety, Workshop Technical Capability & Customer Satisfaction

    Position Overview

    The Diagnostic Expert (DE) is responsible for advanced diagnosis and structured troubleshooting of complex mechanical, electrical, electronic, software-related, and high-voltage concerns in hybrid, electric (EV/PHEV), and internal-combustion-engine (ICE) passenger vehicles, in accordance with applicable brand repair procedures.

    The role converts customer-reported symptoms and workshop observations into a systematic diagnostic approach; validates findings through measured data, diagnostic records, and approved test procedures; and supports accurate root-cause identification. The Diagnostic Expert guides technicians on complex cases, supports technical escalation where required, and contributes to avoiding unnecessary component replacement through evidence-based fault isolation using established diagnostic flow chart and approved OEM procedures.

    The DE also supports workshop technical capability through case-based coaching, technical-learning documentation, and communication of relevant technical observations to the Workshop Controller and Service Advisor for appropriate customer communication. The role operates strictly within its formal high-voltage training, certification, and authorization boundaries, and does not independently make customer-cost, warranty, repair-approval, or vehicle-release decisions unless such authority is formally delegated.

    1. Education

    Diploma or Degree in Automobile Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Electronics Engineering, or related technical discipline.OEM technical certification or training in high-voltage EV/hybrid/ICE vehicle diagnostics is preferred.

    2. Experience

    4–6 years of experience in automotive diagnosis and troubleshooting in an authorized passenger-vehicle workshop.Hands-on experience in EV, PHEV, hybrid, ICE-vehicle diagnostics, diagnostic scan-tool usage, and electrical-circuit testing is preferred.Experience in handling intermittent faults, repeat repairs, technical escalations, and cases requiring coordination with OEM field or remote technical support is preferred.

    3. Key Responsibilities

    A. Complex-Concern Review and Diagnostic Planning
    • Review customer concerns, repair orders, technician observations, and available diagnostic findings to assess complex technical cases.
    • Work with the Service Advisor to check and validate issues reported by the customer, in line with the Aftersales SOP.
    • Where appropriate, join the Service Advisor for a short test drive to assess the reported concern and determine whether diagnosis in the interactive bay is required.
    • Translate the customer’s concern into a clear and factual symptom statement before beginning a detailed diagnosis.
    • Reproduce the reported condition/concern wherever possible, following approved safety and test-drive procedures.
    • Define a structured, step-by-step diagnostic plan before dismantling components or recommending part replacement.
    • Use approved manufacturer troubleshooting procedures, diagnostic trees/flowchart, service information, and available repair history to support root-cause identification.
    • Review diagnostic evidence critically and avoid trial-based repair recommendations that are not supported by testing or approved procedures.
    • Ensure Right-First-Time diagnosis and repairs for concerns reported in the customer vehicle.
    B. Diagnostic Testing and Fault Isolation
    • Connect and operate approved OEM diagnostic scan tools and relevant test equipment to access diagnostic trouble codes (DTCs), live data, freeze-frame data, and other available diagnostic information.
    • Perform appropriate electrical checks while protecting sensitive vehicle electronic modules.
    • Diagnose mechanical, electrical, electronic, communication, software, and control-module-related concerns within the role’s approved technical competence.
    • Document diagnostic observations, test results, fault-isolation logic, and recommend next actions in the applicable job-card, repair-order, or technical-record process.
    • Communicate the required repair scope, technical dependency, risk, and estimated diagnostic or repair timelines to the Workshop Controller for workshop planning.
    C. EV/PHEV and High-Voltage Diagnostic Support
    • Diagnose EV/PHEV and hybrid-vehicle concerns—including electric motors, inverters, power electronics, and DC-DC converters—in accordance with approved high-voltage safety procedures and within the role’s training, authorization level, and approved competence and process boundaries.
    • Confirm that safe high-voltage de-energization and zero-voltage verification are completed through the approved process before critical high-voltage repair work begins.
    • Immediately stop work or escalate concerns involving suspected high-voltage or battery damage, missing safety controls, unsafe conditions, unclear repair methods, or work outside the technician’s authorization.
    D. Software, Programming and Technical Repair Support
    • Support software updates, control-module programming or flashing, and diagnosis of communication or programming faults supported by applicable tools and procedures.
    • Guide technicians through approved diagnostic trees/flowchart, test methods, repair procedures, and evidence-based fault-isolation steps.
    • Support the Workshop Controller in planning complex diagnostic work, including equipment, bay, time, technician, technical support, and safety dependencies.
    • Communicate technically accurate findings, required repair actions and realistic timelines to the Workshop Controller and Service Advisor for appropriate customer communication.
    E. Post-Repair Verification and Technical Case Closure
    • Perform or support post-repair verification to confirm that the diagnosed concern/s has been addressed.
    • Carry out applicable functional checks, DTC clearing and rechecking, calibration, charging validation, and road testing in accordance with approved procedures
    • Confirm that relevant diagnostic results and repair evidence are documented before the vehicle proceeds to final quality checks and delivery stages.
    • Identify repeat concerns, incomplete fault resolution, or unresolved technical issues and ensure they are recorded and escalated through the applicable process.
    F. Technical Escalation and Knowledge Management
    • Escalate recurring, unresolved, or product-related technical concerns to JSW’s Technical Support through the approved channel.
    • Prepare complete technical-escalation documentation, including applicable diagnostic logs, DTCs, test results, repair history, photographs, observations, and work already performed.
    • Maintain a workshop technical-learning log covering repeat failures, complex, critical diagnosis, repair solutions, technical bulletins, and lessons learned, and share relevant findings and approved updates with fellow technicians and the Workshop Controller.
    • Support technical trend analysis for repeat repairs, recurring DTCs, quality concerns, or unresolved cases.
    G. Capability Building, Equipment and Process Compliance
    • Conduct case-based coaching and on-the-job training to strengthen technicians’ diagnostic capability, electrical-circuit-testing practices, and EV/PHEV safety awareness.
    • Identify recurring skill gaps and communicate technician development needs to the Workshop Controller or Service Manager through the appropriate process.
    • Follow applicable diagnostic equipment calibration, software update, tool-control, workshop safety, 5S, documentation, and brand-process requirements.

    4. Key Performance Indicators (KPIs)

    Diagnostic Accuracy and Repair Quality
    • Fix-Right-First Time / First Time-Right diagnostic performance
    • Repeat repair and comeback rate for diagnosed vehicles
    • Percentage of complex cases supported by complete diagnostic evidence and root-cause documentation
    Turnaround Time and Technical Support
    • Diagnostic turnaround time per vehicle or assigned case
    • Ageing of open diagnostic cases

    5. Key Competencies

    Advanced vehicle-diagnosis and systematic fault-isolation capabilityElectrical wiring-diagram interpretation and electrical-circuit testingProficiency with approved OEM diagnostic tools, multimeters, oscilloscopes, and insulation-test equipment.Knowledge of EV/hybrid powertrain systems and applicable high-voltage safety requirementsHigh-voltage hazard recognition, risk assessment, controlled isolation, and emergency-response awarenessRoot-cause analysis, hypothesis testing, evidence-based decision-making, and diagnostic attention to detailTechnical documentation, diagnostic-record interpretation, and structured OEM case preparationSoftware, communication, programming, and control-module fault-awarenessPost-repair verification, calibration, charging validation, and applicable road-test capabilityClear technical communication and technician-coaching capabilityCross-functional coordination with Service Advisors, Workshop Controller, Quality Control, Parts, Warranty, and OEM-support channelsCustomer-focused judgement, especially in repeat-repair, vehicle-down, safety-related, and escalated casesProcess discipline, safe-work orientation, and brand-value alignment

    Electrical Expert

    DepartmentAfter Sales – Workshop
    Reporting toWorkshop Controller
    Role ImpactElectrical System Diagnosis and Troubleshooting, First-Time-Fix, EV/PHEV Electrical Safety, Workshop Technical Capability & Customer Satisfaction

    Position Overview

    The Electrical Expert is responsible for inspecting, diagnosing, and repairing vehicle electrical and electronic systems in accordance with OEM repair procedures and the role of training and authorization.

    The role translates reported symptoms into a structured diagnostic approach, identifies faults through circuit testing and measured evidence, and verifies repairs before submitting the vehicle for the prescribed quality checks. It supports vehicle reliability through correct wiring-harness repair, component testing, and accurate technical documentation rather than trial-based component replacement.

    The Electrical Expert coordinates with the Diagnostic Expert and Workshop Controller on complex, intermittent, repeat, and safety-related concerns.

    1. Education

    ITI or Diploma in Electrical, Electronics, Automobile, or Mechanical Engineering.Advanced training or certification in EV/PHEV electrical diagnosis and repair is preferred.

    2. Experience

    2 to 5 years of experience in automotive electrical repairs and troubleshooting in an authorized passenger vehicle workshop.Experience in EV/PHEV electrical systems, wiring harness repair, and electronic accessories is preferred.

    3. Key Responsibilities

    • Review the repair order, reported symptoms, and available repair history, and verify the concern before commencing diagnosis.
    • Inspect, trace, and repair automotive electrical circuits, wiring harnesses, connectors, and grounding points using multi-meters and test equipment.
    • Use wiring diagrams, connector views, terminal numbers, fuse/relay layouts, pin-out data, and OEM repair instructions to plan and perform electrical fault tracing safely and systematically.
    • Follow a structured electrical diagnostic tree: verify the reported symptoms, check DTCs and freeze frame data where available, inspect power/ground/fuse conditions, test the relevant circuit, complete the repairs, and carry out post repair validation.
    • Inspect wiring harnesses for chafing, stretching, pinching, heat damage, corrosion, loose retention, poor routing, water ingress, rodent damage, and previous non-standard repairs; restore the harness using OEM-approved repair methods.
    • Inspect and repair vehicle charging systems, AC/DC charge ports, lock actuators, and high-voltage interlock lines as per service manuals.
    • Test, maintain, and replace auxiliary 12V/48V batteries and troubleshoot DC-DC converters powering onboard electrical systems.
    • Diagnose and repair electronic systems including infotainment, power windows, central locking, and automatic climate control.
    • Check and calibrate sensors, cameras, and driver assistance (ADAS) units following body repairs, windshield replacement, or wheel alignment.
    • Follow wiring harness routing guidelines to prevent wiring damage, short circuits or moisture ingress.
    • Coordinate with the Workshop Controller and Diagnostic Expert for complex electrical faults and repair timelines.
    • Follow all workshop high-voltage safety precautions and PPE requirements.
    • Escalate intermittent, repeat, safety-related, network, high-voltage-interface, programming, and unresolved electrical concerns with a complete technical handover to Workshop controller.
    • Immediately report damaged high-voltage insulation, exposed conductors, thermal events, water intrusion near high-voltage components, or suspected isolation faults; secure the work area and follow the workshop escalation process.
    • Maintain electrical test equipment, scan-tool interfaces, battery support units, and special service tools in calibrated, serviceable, and safely stored condition.
    • Ensure clean work practices, tool maintenance, and adherence to 5S in the electrical repair bay.

    4. Key Performance Indicators (KPIs)

    Quality & Technical Performance
    • Repeat (Internal/ External) / Rework %
    • Turnaround time (TAT)
    • Average Diagnosis resolution time
    • Technical Escalation: Number of issues resolved without OEM escalation.
    Productivity
    • Electrician productivity and efficiency
    • Job completion within committed time
    • Bay Productivity

    5. Key Competencies

    Automotive circuit tracing, wiring harness repair, and soldering/crimping skillsKnowledge of low-voltage and auxiliary EV/hybrid electrical architecturesAbility to read electrical wiring diagrams and use multi-meters and circuit testersUnderstanding of sensor calibration and vehicle electronicsTechnical expertise in vehicle diagnosis, troubleshooting & problem-solving ability5S & Safety awareness when working near high-voltage wiring and componentsWillingness to learn new vehicle technologies and repair proceduresUnderstanding of RO, repair manuals and technical proceduresDigital literacy needed, updating tech comment on a tablet / PC, work start and stop over workshop App or PC.Basic understanding of CAN/LIN communication circuits, module power/ground checks, and escalation requirements for complex network concernsKnowledge of workshop tools and diagnostic equipmentTime management and ability to meet job timelinesTeamwork and coordination with workshop colleaguesBasic communication skills

    Trainee Technician

    DepartmentAfter Sales – Workshop
    Reporting toWorkshop Controller / Senior Technician
    Role ImpactService Support, Learning Progress, Workshop 5S & Safety Adherence

    Position Overview

    The Trainee Technician is responsible for supporting senior technicians in vehicle inspection, periodic maintenance, and general repair work while learning dealership workshop operations and brand standards. The role assists in basic servicing, tool management, and bay cleanliness while following safety rules to build automotive repair skills.

    The Trainee Technician must recognize high voltage hazard boundaries and must not de-energize, diagnose, disconnect, repair, probe, or handle high voltage systems, battery packs, or restricted components unless appropriately trained, authorized, and instructed.

    1. Education

    ITI or Diploma in Automobile, Mechanical, or Electrical Engineering (recent pass-out or apprentice).

    2. Experience

    0 to 1 year of apprenticeship or basic workshop training in an automotive environment.Eagerness to learn about passenger car servicing, mechanical repairs, and EV/hybrid technologies.

    • Maintain cleanliness in the service bay, ensuring floors are clean, dry, oil free, and compliant with 5S standards.
    • Review assigned job cards, service instructions, and required tools with the senior technician before starting work.
    • Apply steering, seat, floor, and fender covers before servicing, noting any preexisting vehicle marks or damage.
    • Follow inspection checklists methodically and verify findings with senior staff before taking corrective action.
    • Operate vehicle lifts and tire equipment only after receiving proper training, approval, and direct supervision.
    • Inspect hand tools and measuring devices before using, reporting damaged or uncalibrated tools right away.
    • Verify replacement parts, part numbers, and fluid grades against the job card under senior guidance.
    • Organize removed fasteners and parts neatly on trays to prevent mixing up, loss, or fluid contamination.

    • Respect EV and PHEV safety boundaries, warning signs, and restricted high voltage bays at all times.

    • Record task completion, used consumables, and learning points in the training log after every job.
    • Participate actively in morning meetings, technical demos, and 5S cleanliness routines.
    • Dispose of drained oil, old filters, used fluids, and scrap parts in designated environmental bins.

    • Attend internal technical training sessions, read manufacturer service manuals, and complete assigned learning modules diligently.
    • Follow instructions from the Workshop Controller and senior technicians accurately and respectfully.

    Warranty Specialist

    DepartmentAftersales – Warranty
    Reporting toService Manager
    Role ImpactWarranty Claim Quality, submission & approval Support, Compliance, Cost Recovery, Financial Reconciliation and Customer Satisfaction

    Position Overview

    The Warranty Specialist is responsible for administering and controlling the dealership warranty-claim process in accordance with JSW’s warranty policy. The role reviews repair documentation and vehicle history for warranty coverage, identifies documentation gaps, prepares warranty submissions, tracks claim status, coordinates required approvals, maintains failed-part storage with appropriate tagging, PRC (Parts return center) returns/ disposal as per OEM policy, and supports reconciliation of approved warranty settlements.

    The role works closely with Service Advisors, Workshop Controller, Diagnostic Expert, technicians, Parts, Accounts, Service Manager, and relevant OEM warranty teams to ensure that warranty cases are supported by complete, accurate, timely, and traceable documentation. The Warranty Specialist helps reduce avoidable claim queries and rejections, supports audit readiness, and provides feedback to workshop teams on recurring documentation and process gaps.

    The role supports warranty administration by ensuring that required technical evidence, component details, safety documentation, approvals, and failed-part-handling records are available in accordance with the OEMs requirements.

    1. Education

    Graduate or Diploma in Automobile Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or related field is preferred.OEM training or certification in warranty administration, DMS warranty modules, audit compliance, or Car's warranty processes are desirable.

    2. Experience

    5+ years of experience in automotive Aftersales warranty operations.Experience in warranty claim preparation, submission support, tracking, reconciliation, or warranty documentation in an automotive dealership.Experience in warranty-claim submission and reconciliation at an EV passenger-vehicle dealership is preferred.Exposure to complex claims involving high-voltage batteries, drive units, power electronics, charging systems, software-related repairs, repeat repairs, or technical escalations is preferred.

    3. Key Responsibilities

    A. Warranty Eligibility Review and Claim Identification
    • Review repair orders, vehicle history, applicable warranty details, and available repair documentation to identify potential warranty cases.
    • Check claim eligibility against the applicable warranty policy, including relevant warranty type, vehicle information, repair context, and required conditions.
    • Support the Service Advisor and Service Manager with operational clarification of documentation and policy requirements for warranty cases.
    • Distinguish between jobs eligible under warranty, customer-payable jobs, goodwill requests, and other claim categories in accordance with applicable policy and warranty processes.
    • Keep abreast of development in the Warranty Policies / Warranty manuals and documentation guidelines and disseminate it to dealership staff from time to time.
    • Understand the Audit criteria's & requirements, keep the documentation & the evidence in line with the guidelines
    B. Documentation Review and Claim Preparations
    • Obtain and review the required supporting information from relevant workshop personnel, including customer concern, diagnosis, repair order, technician comments, photographs, diagnostic records, parts details, and other applicable evidence.
    • Identify incomplete, inconsistent, unclear, or unsupported documentation before claim submission or approval processing.
    • Prepare or support preparation of prior-approval requests where required by applicable warranty policy.
    • Prepare & review, claim submissions in the approved warranty system/DMS, also ensuring that labour operations & codes, parts information, causal-part details, defect and symptom codes, repair narrative, tax treatment, and supporting attachments are selected and documented accurately.
    C. Claim Submission, Approval Tracking and Status Coordination
    • Track and monitor claims from prior approval through submission, query resolution, approval, settlement, and closure.
    • Monitor claim status, pending approvals, OEM queries, rejected claims, resubmissions, and ageing cases. Follow up for pending claims/ queries with appropriate internal/OEM channels.
    • Coordinate the response to rejected submissions by obtaining accurate technical or repair documentation from relevant teams and support re-submission.
    • Update Service Advisors and the Service Manager on claim-status changes for accurate customer communication.
    • Escalate overdue approvals, recurring claim queries, high-value discrepancies, repeat rejections, or process barriers to the Service Manager.
    D. Warranty Settlement, Reconciliation and Financial Control
    • Track and reconcile approved claim amounts vs submitted claims, credit notes, claim settlements, outstanding claims, and payment confirmation in coordination with Accounts.
    • Identify and immediately flag discrepancies between submitted, approved, credited, rejected, or settled amounts to the Service Manager and Accounts team.
    • Maintain records of pending, paid, partially settled, rejected, and closed claims in the approved tracking process.
    • Support timely closure of financial and documentation actions relating to warranty settlements.
    E. Failed-Part Management and Traceability
    • Ensure failed parts are identified, tagged, segregated, stored, and handled in accordance with applicable OEM and dealership requirements.
    • Coordinate the availability of approved part-return tags, and supporting records as per the designated process.
    • Maintain traceability between the warranty claim, repair order, causal part, failed part, part-return documentation, and final disposal or return status.
    • Coordinate failed-part return to the manufacturer and maintain complete records of failed-part return, retention, quarantine, scrap, or disposal activity as per SOP,
    • Escalate missing, incorrectly tagged, damaged, non-traceable, or non-compliant failed-part cases promptly.
    F. Warranty-Case Administration
    • Maintain working awareness of applicable warranty terms, documentation requirements, and evidence expectations for covered repairs.
    • For high-voltage component claims, confirm that required technical authorization, safety-checklist records, photographs, component serial numbers, and diagnostic evidence are available before progressing the claim.
    • Confirm that applicable manufacturer requirements for packaging, quarantine, dangerous-goods documentation, failed-part return, and special handling are addressed through the responsible, authorized teams.
    G. Audit Readiness, Continuous Improvement and Reporting
    • Conduct periodic self-reviews of open, rejected, paid, and closed claims to identify any documentation, process, financial-reconciliation, or traceability gaps and apply corrective actions on identified gaps before an OEM or internal warranty audit.
    • Maintain complete, accurate, and readily traceable records for audits, claim checks, policy reviews, and management reporting.
    • Analyse recurring claim rejection reasons, documentation errors, missing evidence, failed-part non-compliance, and process gaps.
    • Support coaching or awareness sessions on warranty-documentation discipline, claim evidence, failed-part control, and common rejection-prevention practices with the workshop team.
    • Provide periodic reports to the Service Manager on claim volume, approvals, rejection trends, pending claims, ageing, settlement status, recovery, failed-part compliance, audit findings, and corrective-action status.

    • Claim-status tracking completeness

    Position Overview

    The Quality Controller is responsible for supporting effective workshop job planning and verifying the quality of completed repair work before vehicle release. The role reviews job requirements, repair orders, customer concerns, technician notes, and relevant diagnostic information to ensure that approved work has been completed and that identified concerns have been appropriately addressed.

    The Quality Controller manages the quality-inspection and recheck process, records defects or gaps, and coordinates the return of vehicles for correction where required. This role contributes to First Time-Right performance, vehicle safety, on-time delivery, and customer confidence in completed repairs.

    5–6 years of experience in passenger-vehicle servicing, repairs, workshop quality checks, or related workshop operations.Experience in final inspection, road testing (holding valid Driving license), diagnostic-record review, and repair-quality verification is preferred.Experience in an EV passenger-vehicle workshop is preferred.

    3. Key Responsibilities

    A. Repair-Order and Pre-Inspection Review
    • Review the repair order, approved job scope, customer concerns, technician notes, and relevant diagnostic records before inspecting the vehicle.
    • Confirm that the vehicle is presented for inspection after completion of the approved repair work.
    • Identify the relevant inspection points based on the customer concern, repair work completed, and applicable quality-check requirements.
    • Use the approved quality checklist and available diagnostic records while conducting inspection activities.
    B. Final Inspection, Road Test and Quality Verification
    • Inspect the vehicle to verify that approved repair work has been completed and the vehicle is in an appropriate condition for the next stage of the delivery process.
    • Verify repair quality against applicable workshop and brand-quality requirements.
    • Carry out a road test, where required and appropriate, to check for NVH, repeat concerns, and other relevant vehicle-performance observations.
    • Identify incomplete work, defects, unresolved customer concerns, or quality gaps found during inspection or road testing.
    • Record failed inspection points clearly and return the vehicle to the Workshop Controller for correction.
    • Reinspect the vehicle after corrective work has been completed.
    • Release the vehicle for washing only after applicable checks have passed.
    • Report safety concerns immediately and ensure the vehicle is not released for the next stage until the concern has been resolved through the appropriate process.
    C. Defect Documentation, Rework Control and Improvement
    • Maintain accurate inspection reports, quality-check records, rejection details, and recheck outcomes.
    • Maintain technician-wise quality-rejection records to enable review of recurring quality gaps.
    • Track internal quality rejections, repeat repairs, rework, and First-Time-Right performance trends.
    • Share repeated faults, quality trends, and recurring repair concerns with the Service Manager and workshop team.
    • Provide clear, factual, and constructive feedback to relevant workshop personnel on observed defects and required corrective action.
    • Support corrective action and follow-up for recurring quality issues, without independently altering repair methods or technical procedures unless formally authorized.
    D. Safety, EV/PHEV and Process Compliance
    • Follow applicable workshop-quality procedures, brand requirements, and safety practices during inspection and road testing.
    • Apply appropriate precautions when inspecting EV/PHEV vehicles, in line with approved procedures.
    • Escalate EV/PHEV, high-voltage, battery, safety, or technical concerns to trained and authorized personnel.
    • Do not independently diagnose, repair, or authorize high-voltage work beyond the role’s approved competence and process scope.
    • Maintain timely, accurate, and complete quality-related documentation in the approved records and systems.

    4. Key Performance Indicators (KPIs)

    Quality and First-Time-Right Performance
    • Final inspection completion before vehicle delivery
    • Internal quality-rejection rate
    • Repeat Complaint rate
    • First-Time-Right / Fix-Right-First-Time performance
    • Road test %
    • Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) compliance
    • Diagnostic/Final Inspector’s Report Accuracy
    Customer Experience and Safety
    • Customer feedback related to completed repair work

    5. Key Competencies

This includes coordinating PDI work, accessory fitment (if required), vehicle condition checks, transit-damage recording, rectification coordination, final inspection, documentation, and release-status communication.

    The PDI In-charge supervises the PDI, and accessory-fitment technician assigned to the team, maintains visibility of vehicle readiness against planned delivery priorities, and ensures that no vehicle is released with an identified unresolved concern.

Ensure that vehicle-preservation activity is recorded through the approved checklist, register, or system.

    Position Overview

    The Technician - PDI & AXS is responsible for carrying out Pre-Delivery Inspection (PDI) and installing genuine accessories on new vehicles as per brand specifications. The role ensures that every vehicle is thoroughly inspected, cosmetically clean, technically checked, and equipped with approved accessories prior to customer delivery, supporting zero-defect handovers and high customer satisfaction.

    Position Overview

    The Washing Supervisor is responsible for planning, supervising, and controlling vehicle washing, cleaning, mopping, detailing, and pre-delivery cleanliness-inspection activities in accordance with brand standards.

    The role manages the movement of vehicles through washing bays, allocates work to washing personnel, monitors wash quality, and ensures that vehicles are cleaned through an approved and controlled process. This includes use of appropriate cleaning materials, safe washing practices, controlled water pressure, customer-vehicle-protection measures, cleanliness inspection, and timely escalation of vehicle-condition, safety, quality, or delivery-readiness concerns.

    The Washing Supervisor supports efficient vehicle flow from workshop or bodyshop completion through cleaning, inspection and handover readiness, while safeguarding vehicle condition, customer belongings, and EV/PHEV-sensitive areas.

    1. Education

    10th or 12th pass, or Diploma in any discipline.Training in automotive detailing, vehicle-care processes, 5S, workplace safety, or EV/PHEV washing precautions is desirable.

    2. Experience

    2–4 years of experience in automotive vehicle washing, detailing, wash-bay operations, or washing-bay supervision in an authorized dealership or detailing center.Experience in vehicle-cleanliness inspection, wash-quality control, vehicle-movement coordination, material use, and washing equipment handling.Exposure to EV/PHEV washing precautions, sensor and camera protection, charge-port care, water-management practices, and dealership pre-delivery inspection processes is preferred.

    3. Key Responsibilities

    • Plan and organize vehicle washing queues based on workshop or bodyshop completion status, priority requirements, and customer-delivery commitments.
    • Maintain smooth movement of vehicles through washing, mopping, detailing, inspection and delivery-readiness stages.

    • Maintain a visible wash-status board, register or other approved tracking method.:
    • Identify washing-capacity, manpower, weather, equipment, vehicle-condition, or workflow constraints that may affect customer-delivery commitments.
    • Check for customer belongings in the vehicle and protect them in accordance with the dealership’s approved lost-property, key-control, and escalation procedures.
    • Protect repaired areas, fresh paint, exposed components, and other identified sensitive areas in accordance with approved washing (dry/wet washing), and escalate unsafe vehicle conditions, visible damage, exposed connectors, loose parts, unresolved repair concerns, or unclear handling instructions before commencing washing.

    • Conduct a structured pre-delivery cleanliness and vehicle-condition inspection using the approved checklist or check sheet.
    • Record wash-inspection results, rewash status, and unresolved concerns in a designated tracking method.
    • Monitor washer performance, wash-quality consistency, bay cycle times, rewash causes, material usage, equipment downtime, and daily output.
    • Provide OJT to washing staff on safe wash methods, chemical handling, microfiber discipline, vehicle protection, EV/PHEV precautions, quality standards, and correct equipment use.
    • Monitor the condition and daily upkeep of washing equipment, including pressure washers, vacuum cleaners, air compressors, water-drainage systems, and related wash-bay equipment.
    • Report equipment failures, unsafe equipment conditions, drainage concerns, or maintenance needs that may affect quality, safety, or workflow.
    • Track and maintain adequate availability of washing shampoos, microfiber towels, polishes, cleaning consumables, and other approved materials.
    • Maintain clean, dry, organized, and slip-free washing-bay surroundings in accordance with dealership safety and 5S standards.

    Position Overview

    The Washer is responsible for washing, drying, vacuuming, and cleaning customer and dealership vehicles to the approved cleanliness standards.

    The role supports customer delivery readiness through thorough cleaning, careful handling of vehicle surfaces and interiors, and timely completion of assigned work. It protects vehicles and customer belongings by using approved materials and equipment, observing EV/PHEV washing precautions, and promptly reporting damage, abnormal conditions, or safety concerns.

    1. Education

    10th pass or basic vocational training.Basic training in vehicle washing, interior cleaning, chemical handling, equipment use, and workplace safety is desirable.

    3. Key Responsibilities

    • Carry out assigned cleaning work according to the Washing Supervisor’s priorities and delivery requirements.

    • Dry the exterior, glass, mirrors and other permitted areas thoroughly using clean microfiber towels and compressed air blowers to prevent water marks and residual dripping.

Coordinate with the Washing Supervisor on priority vehicles, delivery timing, rewash requirements, and bay availability.
