    Bodyshop SA

    DepartmentAftersales – Body Shop
    Reporting toBody Shop Manager
    Role ImpactCustomer Experience, Repair Estimation, Insurance Coordination, Repair Progress and Vehicle Delivery

    Position Overview

    The Body Shop Service Advisor is the primary customer-facing representative and single point of contact throughout the accident repair process. The role is responsible for damage assessment, repair estimation, insurance coordination, and regular communication with customers and surveyors regarding repair status, costs, and delivery timelines. The Service Advisor works closely with the Body Shop Controller to ensure smooth and timely repair execution.

    1. Education

    Graduate Or Diploma in Automobile or Mechanical EngineeringProfessional certification with other OEM is preferred

    2. Experience

    4 years of experience in automotive bodyshop operations and insurance claim handling.Familiarity with DMS/ Dealer Management Systems and basic Body Shop KPI tracking is preferredGood Understanding of Accidental Vehicle Operation, Insurance Coordination, Workshop operations, warranty & Parts Co-Ordination.

    3. Key Responsibilities

    A. Customer Reception, Vehicle Inspection and Job-Card Preparation
    • Welcome customers professionally and with empathy, particularly in accident repair or vehicle damage situations.
    • Understand, record, and clarify the customer’s reported vehicle damage, repair requirements, and concerns.
    • Inspect the vehicle with the customer and accurately document visible damage and relevant observations.
    • Create or support creation of the job card in accordance with the approved dealership process and after required customer approval.
    • Ensure damage details, customer requirements, labour requirements, parts requirements, and repair-related information are recorded accurately in the DMS.
    • Explain the initial repair process, expected approvals, documentation requirements, and next steps to the customer clearly.
    B. Estimate Preparation and Customer Approval (Critical in Cash repairs)
    • Prepare or coordinate preparation of repair estimates, including required labour, parts, and other applicable repair requirements using DMS/Estimation creation tool (if available).
    • Review the repair estimate with the customer & Insurance surveyor and explain the scope of work, expected costs, conditions, and indicative delivery commitment.
    • Seek and document customer approval before undertaking additional repairs, changes in repair scope, or supplementary estimates.
    • Inform & Coordinate with customer promptly where additional work, changes in cost, part non-availability, or revised delivery timelines affect the original understanding.
    • Maintain appropriate documentation of Insurance & customer communication, estimate revisions, and approval status.
    C. Insurance and Surveyor Coordination
    • Guide customers on the insurance documents required for normal and cashless claims, within the defined dealership process.
    • Coordinate claim-intimation, surveyor inspection, repair-estimate review, and approval-related activities with the insurance company and surveyor.
    • Coordinate with customers and surveyors for supplementary approvals where required.
    • Track insurance-approval status and follow up on pending surveyor or insurer actions that may affect repair commencement or vehicle delivery.
    • Coordinate for final approval or Delivery Order (DO), final photos, where applicable for insurance repairs.
    • Maintain and verify relevant insurance-claim documentation before delivery, in coordination with the internal teams.
    D. Repair Progress, Parts and Delivery Coordination
    • Track daily repair progress with the Bodyshop Controller, Body Shop Manager, workshop team, Parts team, and insurance surveyor.
    • Monitor parts availability, pending parts, and repair dependencies that may affect vehicle turnaround time.
    • Communicate expected delays, revised repair status, additional work requirements, and revised delivery expectations to customers proactively.
    • Update customers at appropriate stages of the repair journey and respond to reasonable customer requests for progress information.
    • Support coordination of parts requirements and Vehicle Off Road (VOR) part requests, where applicable under the approved process.
    • Work with internal teams to reduce avoidable delays and support the achievement of committed delivery timelines.
    E. Vehicle Delivery and Customer Handover
    • Before vehicle delivery, coordinate checks of repair completion, available insurance documentation, invoice status, vehicle cleanliness, and delivery readiness.
    • Support quality verification through the quality control process; do not independently certify repair quality unless formally authorized.
    • Explain completed repair work, invoice or payment-related information, and relevant vehicle delivery details to the customer.
    • Address open customer concerns and coordinate escalation of unresolved matters to the Body Shop Manager or Workshop team.
    • Escort or guide the customer through vehicle handover in accordance with the approved delivery process.
    • Ensure relevant job-card, billing, delivery, and customer-interaction records are updated in the DMS.
    F. Customer Feedback, Concern Resolution and Process Discipline
    • Capture customer concerns, repair-related feedback, and relevant customer communication accurately.
    • Support customer-concern resolution by coordinating with the appropriate workshop, CRM, insurance, or Senior management.
    • Record relevant actions, customer interactions, root-cause details, and resolution status in the applicable CRM or dealership process where assigned.
    • Escalate customer dissatisfaction, repeat concerns, delayed repairs, approval of bottlenecks, and unresolved cases in a timely manner.
    • Follow dealership processes, brand standards, data-privacy requirements, and professional customer-handling practices at all times.
    G. EV/PHEV Accident-Vehicle Awareness
    • Maintain basic awareness of damaged EV/PHEV vehicle safety considerations and high-voltage escalation requirements.
    • Escalate EV/PHEV accident vehicle safety, technical, battery, charging, or high-voltage concerns to HV trained and authorized personnel.
    • Do not provide technical safety advice or authorize handling of damaged high-voltage vehicles outside the assigned role and approved process.

    4. Key Performance Indicators (KPIs)

    Customer Experience
    • Customer Satisfaction Index (CSI) / Net Promoter Score (NPS)
    Workshop and Revenue Contribution
    • Labour sales per Repair Order (RO)
    • Parts sales per Repair Order (RO)
    • Value-Added Sales per Repair Order (RO)
    • Accessories and extended-service business
    • Body-to-Mechanical conversion
    Process, Delivery and Quality
    • Insurance process TAT
    • Vehicle turnaround time (TAT)
    • On-time delivery: promised delivery date versus actual delivery date
    • Repeat-repair and rework percentage

    5. Key Competencies

    Empathy and professionalism in handling customers facing vehicle damage or accident-related distressClear, patient, and customer-focused verbal and written communicationActive listening, probing, and accurate concern captureVehicle-damage documentation and attention to detailBody-repair estimate, and repair-scope awarenessInsurance-claims, surveyor-coordination, and approval-process and Insurance rules awarenessJob-card and repair-progress process knowledgeCustomer-objection handling and concern escalationRepair-status and delivery-commitment communicationCross-functional coordination with Bodyshop, Parts, insurance, and customer-relations teamsPlanning, follow-up, scheduling, and task-management disciplineDMS and applicable customer-record system proficiencyBusiness awareness and consultative-selling capabilityBasic awareness of EV/PHEV accident-vehicle safety and high-voltage escalation requirementsBrand-value orientation

    Bodyshop Controller

    DepartmentAftersales – Body Shop
    Reporting toBody Shop Manager
    Role ImpactBodyshop Workflow Control, Productivity, Repair Turnaround Time (TAT), Repair Quality, Safety and Customer Satisfaction

    Position Overview

    The Bodyshop Controller is responsible for planning, allocating, monitoring, and controlling the flow of accident vehicles through the body shop. The role maintains real-time, bay-wise and vehicle-wise visibility of repair status and coordinates with the Body Shop Manager and Service Advisor to ensure efficient job allocation based on technician skills, available resources, approved repair processes, and committed delivery timelines.

    1. Education

    Diploma or Degree in Automobile Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, a related discipline.Professional certification (JC Certification) with other OEM is preferred

    2. Experience

    7 years of experience in automotive bodyshop operations, accident-repair supervision, or related bodyshop workflow-control activity in an authorized passenger-vehicle dealership.Good understanding of OEM body repair procedures, accident repair processes, quality standards, safety requirements, and workshop operating practices.Hands-on experience in job planning, technician and bay allocation, vehicle movement, repair-stage monitoring, and on-time delivery management.

    3. Key Responsibilities

    A. Daily Bodyshop Planning and Work-in-Progress Control
    • Conduct a daily bodyshop review covering estimate and approval status, vehicles awaiting survey, carry-over cases, current repair stage, technician and bay availability, parts status/escalations for PNA cases, delivery commitments, and safety or technical escalations.
    • Maintain current and accurate visibility of every work-in-progress vehicle through the approved bodyshop control board, repair-management system, tablet, or dashboard.
    • Track vehicle status, repair-stage ageing, hold reason, promised delivery date, next action, responsible person, and required escalation for each active vehicle.
    • Review planned work against available body and paint capacity, technician capability, bay availability, equipment availability, and delivery commitments.
    • Monitor daily planned output against actual output and identify vehicles requiring action to prevent avoidable carryover or ageing.
    • Escalate capacity constraints, bottlenecks, and delivery risks to the Body Shop Manager in a timely manner.
    B. Repair Planning, Allocation and Stage Control
    • Allocate vehicles and repair operations across the applicable repair stages, including mechanical strip, body-panel repair, paint preparation, booth spraying, reassembly, quality check, and delivery readiness.
    • Apply skill-matrix and certification-based allocation principles to match repair work with an appropriately capable body and paint technician.
    • Consider repair complexity, structural-repair requirements, material-specific repair requirements, welding, bonding, riveting, paint requirements, HV considerations, diagnostic needs, calibration & special-tool requirements, as well as physical workspace constraints when planning work.
    • Coordinate repair sequencing to reduce unnecessary vehicle movement, avoid waiting between repair stages, minimize duplicate dismantling, and prevent bottlenecks in the body and paint sections.
    • Confirm that relevant repair information, parts, tools, workspace, equipment, and supporting personnel are available before a vehicle progresses to the next repair stage.
    • Monitor technician productivity, productive labour hours, and bay utilization across body and paint operations.
    C. Estimate, Supplementary Damage and Approval Coordination
    • Ensure that additional damage identified during dismantling or repair is inspected, photographed, documented, and routed through the Bodyshop Advisor for customer and surveyor approval before further work proceeds.
    • Coordinate surveyor inspections and approval requirements with complete supporting evidence- photographs (initial, during repair, final), measurement reports, parts details, and technical / repair vs replacement justification where required, and monitor the status of estimates, surveyor review, insurer initial and supplementary approvals, and customer approvals that affect repair commencement or vehicle delivery.
    • Identify and escalate approval delays that present a risk to repair flow, parts ordering, repair start, or committed delivery timing.
    • Maintain appropriate documentation of repair-scope changes, approvals, technical justification, and associated repair-stage status.
    D. Repair Progress, Delivery Delay Risk and Recovery Actions
    • Track repair progress against the planned repair schedule and committed delivery date.
    • Identify delivery-risk cases at an early stage, including delayed insurance approval, supplementary-estimate requirements, hidden damage, parts back-order, structural-repair complexity, technician-capacity constraints, equipment failure, calibration dependency, and EV/PHEV safety holds.
    • Coordinate and communicate any such risks promptly to the Body Shop Manager and relevant teams.
    • Monitor parts availability and coordinate with the Parts team regarding critical, back-ordered, special-order, or repair-blocking parts.
    • Review repair-stage completion before the vehicle proceeds to the next planned stage and support accurate job-status updates and repair-stage documentation in the approved system.
    E. Quality Control, Rework Prevention and Delivery Readiness
    • Ensure that applicable stage-wise quality checks are completed before the vehicle moves to the next repair stage.
    • Monitor internal rework, repeat repairs, paint defects, dimensional deviations, late deliveries, material overruns, customer complaints, and other quality-failure trends.
    • Lead or support root-cause identification for recurring quality and delivery issues, as assigned by the Body Shop Manager.
    • Assign or coordinate corrective and preventive actions with defined process owners and due dates and follow progress through closure.
    • Coordinate post-repair requirements such as wheel alignment, ADAS sensor calibration, diagnostic scans, and functional validation before final handover, where applicable.
    • Ensure that quality-related evidence, repair documentation, measurements, photographs, and delivery-readiness status are complete before the vehicle is presented for final handover stages.
    F. EV/PHEV Collision Repair Planning and Safety Control
    • Confirm that HV safety clearance is obtained through the approved process before bodyshop work begins on hybrid or electric vehicles.
    • Ensure EV/PHEV collision-repair work is assigned only to appropriately trained and authorized personnel.
    • Coordinate with the relevant Service Technician (Body Shop), Diagnostic Expert, Electrical Expert, and OEM technical-support channels (as per availability) for activities such as dismantling, high-voltage isolation, battery handling, thermal-system work, diagnostic checks, programming, calibration, and post-repair functional validation.
    • Escalate suspected battery damage, HV concerns, safety-control gaps, unclear repair methods, or work outside authorized competence without delay, and do not authorize HV, battery, or safety-critical repair work beyond the role’s approved authority.
    G. Tools, Equipment, Workshop Safety and Housekeeping
    • Monitor the availability and safe & working condition of critical bodyshop infrastructure and equipment.
    • Escalate equipment unavailability, required maintenance, calibration requirements, or unsafe equipment conditions that may affect repair quality, safety, or delivery commitments.
    • Enforce compliance with applicable workshop-safety practices, PPE requirements, customer-vehicle-protection standards, and 5S requirements.
    • Maintain standards for key control, safe vehicle movement, fire safety, chemical and waste management, paint-booth ventilation, housekeeping, and material handling.
    • Promote disciplined and safe work practices across the body and paint sections, ensuring proper health of Body & Paint technicians.
    H. Team Coaching and Management Reporting
    • Coach team members on repair-plan discipline, work-status updates, repair documentation, quality checks, customer-vehicle protection, material handling, safe work practices, and timely escalation of repair constraints.
    • Identify recurring skill gaps, process-compliance gaps, and training requirements and raise them with the Body Shop Manager.
    • Provide accurate daily and weekly reporting to the Body Shop Manager
    • Maintain professional bodyshop-floor discipline and compliance with approved dealership, brand, and OEM process requirements.

    4. Key Performance Indicators (KPIs)

    Turnaround Time and Delivery Performance
    • Approval-to-repair-start time
    • Repair-stage adherence against planned timelines
    • Delivery as per promised time
    • Bodyshop vehicle turnaround time (TAT)
    • Daily planned output versus actual output
    • Work-in-progress (WIP) ageing by repair stage
    • Pending RO ratio ((Ratio of daily average pending to monthly load)
    Productivity, Capacity and Quality
    • Bodyshop bay utilization
    • Technician labour efficiency and productive labour utilization
    • Internal rework and repeat-repair performance
    • Paint defects and dimensional-deviation trends
    • Stage-wise quality-check completion
    • Corrective-action closure for quality, rework, and delivery issues
    • Per Panel paint & non paint consumption
    • Material wastage and cost-control adherence
    Safety, Capability and Governance
    • Technician skill-matrix compliance
    • Skill/ Training level Ratios

    5. Key Competencies

    Work-in-progress management, repair-stage tracking, capacity planning, workload balancing, and repair-delivery-risk recoveryBody and paint workflow control, including paint-booth scheduling and bottleneck managementWorking knowledge of OEM collision-repair standards, structural repairability, material-specific repair methods, welding, bonding, riveting, corrosion protection, paint-process controls, and repair-versus-replace decisions.Estimate, supplementary-damage, approval-status, photographic-evidence, and surveyor-coordination awarenessQuality-checkpoint planning, rework prevention, root-cause analysis, corrective-action tracking, and concern closureUnderstanding of vehicle alignment, ADAS calibration, diagnostic-scan, and functional-validation dependenciesEV/PHEV collision-risk awareness, high-voltage and battery-enclosure safety, underbody and thermal-system considerations, authorised allocation, and safe escalationDigital documentation discipline for job cards, stage status, repair photographs, measurements, approvals, material records, quality evidence, and delivery readinessProductivity, efficiency, TAT, labour-time management, WIP-ageing, and capacity-data understanding.Cross-functional coordination with the Body Shop Manager, Bodyshop Advisors, technicians, painters, Parts team, surveyors, and workshop teams.Clear, timely, and professional communication of repair progress, cost or scope changes, technical issues, safety holds, quality concerns, parts constraints, and delivery risksSafety, PPE, housekeeping, chemical or waste-management, and customer-vehicle-care disciplineCoaching ability, sound judgement, composure under delivery pressure, and customer focusProficiency in office and digital tools for communication, data analysis, presentation, and record storageBrand-value orientation

    Body Technician

    DepartmentAftersales – Body Shop
    Reporting toBodyshop Controller
    Role ImpactAccident-Repair Quality, Structural Integrity, Fix-Right-First-Time Performance, EV/PHEV Collision Safety and Customer Satisfaction

    Position Overview

    The Body Technician is responsible for dismantling, repairing, and replacing damaged body and structural components of accident-damaged vehicles in accordance with OEM-recommended repair methods, quality standards, and safety requirements. For EV/PHEV vehicles, the Technician must identify visible collision-related risks and strictly follow OEM-recommended repair procedures.

    1. Education

    ITI or Diploma in Mechanical Engineering, Automobile Engineering, or a related technical discipline.Training or certification in passenger vehicle body repair is desirable.

    2. Experience

    5 years of experience as a Bodyshop Technician in an authorized passenger vehicle Bodyshop.Experience in body repair, panel repair, structural alignment, dismantling, assembly, and fit-and-finish restoration.Experience in EV/PHEV or hybrid-vehicle collision repair is preferred.Understanding Body Repair manuals (Vehicle measurement, Welding technology, Glue & Bonding techniques) used in car, body technical bulletins, job cards and workshop safety practices is an advantage.

    3. Key Responsibilities

    A. Damage Assessment and Repair Preparation
    • Receive repair assignments from the Bodyshop Controller and carefully dismantle damaged parts to assess damage
    • Conduct a detailed pre-repair inspection for hidden or secondary damage affecting other allied parts and relevant repair areas.
    • Identify additional damage, repair constraints, missing information, and parts requirements discovered during dismantling or repair preparation’s
    • Document additional damage with photographs and measurements, parts requirements, and expected delays to the Bodyshop Controller.
    • Assess component repairability against OEM guidelines and communicate to the Bodyshop Controller.
    B. Body, Panel, SMART and Structural Repair
    • Carry out approved body repairs to restore vehicle condition in accordance with the OEM standards.
    • repair damaged body panels and other approved repairable components using appropriate repair tools.
    • Perform structural realignment as per OEM repair procedures using approved (manual and digital) measuring systems.
    • Perform OEM-approved body repairs including (welding, riveting, bonding, Corrosions Protection, SMART repairs, and plastic Repair) to ensure quality repairs, faster turnaround, and enhanced customer satisfaction.
    C. Reassembly, Fit-and-Finish
    • Reassemble repaired or replaced panels and components to meet OEM specifications for (alignment, panel gaps, fit, finish, and secure attachment)
    • Protect sensitive components and adjacent surfaces during repairs to prevent damage to vehicle systems, electronics, and interiors
    D. EV/PHEV Collision Safety and Escalation
    • Inspect EV/PHEV and hybrid vehicles for visible (battery, high-voltage, underbody, and related component damage) promptly escalating and coordinating handover to authorized technical personnel for necessary repairs and calibrations
    E. Stage-Wise Quality Control and Repair & Parts Traceability
    • Conduct stage-wise in-process self-inspections using the quality checklist to verify alignment, fit, corrosion protection, and sealing before proceeding to the next repair stage.
    • Verify completed repairs against quality standards, and job-card requirements, and maintain accurate records of repair activities, findings, work status, photographs, and technical observations.
    • Ensure stage-wise repair quality, escalate unresolved quality or safety concerns, and securely tag, store, & removed or replaced parts against the job card until authorized disposal.
    F. Productivity, Equipment and Workplace Standards
    • Complete assigned repairs within planned timelines, report delays or technical concerns and ensure safe, calibrated, and proper use of tools and equipment.
    • Maintain 5S and workshop safety standards while minimizing material wastage and coordinating with relevant teams for smooth repair flow

    4. Key Performance Indicators (KPIs)

    Repair Quality
    • Number of repair-related rework cases.
    Productivity and Repair Timeliness
    • Technician productivity and efficiency, as defined by the dealership.
    • Completion of work within planned repair-stage timelines.
    Process, Equipment and Compliance
    • Tool, equipment, 5S, safety, and repair-bay audit compliance.

    5. Key Competencies

    Proficiency in panel repair, dent removal, metal finishing, structural damage assessment, and fit-and-finish restoration.Ability to interpret OEM repair manuals, dimensional data, technical bulletins, and approved repair procedures, including the use of digital measuring and pulling systems.Knowledge of welding, riveting, bonding, sealing, corrosion protection, and material-specific repair techniques for steel, plastics.Understanding of EV/PHEV collision safety, high-voltage component protection, restricted repair zones, and the identification and escalation of unsafe or non-repairable components.Strong quality control and documentation skills, including stage-wise inspections, photographic evidence, and repair traceability.Proficiency in safe tool and equipment handling, 5S, workshop safety, time management, teamwork, and cross-functional coordination.

    Paint Technician

    DepartmentAftersales – Body Shop
    Reporting toBodyshop Controller
    Role ImpactPaint-Finish Quality, Bodyshop Productivity, Paint-Material Cost Efficiency, Safety Compliance and Customer Satisfaction

    Position Overview

    The Paint Technician is responsible for Paint Related Work (surface preparation, paint mixing, application, refinishing, and final inspection) of accident-repaired vehicles in accordance with OEM standards, quality requirements, and committed timelines. He ensures proper use of approved paint materials, equipment, and process parameters to achieve accurate colour matching and high-quality finish. The Technician must strictly follow OEM-approved refinishing.

    Education

    ITI, Diploma, or technical certificate in Automotive Painting, Vehicle Refinishing, or related technical discipline.Training in OEM refinishing systems, paint-material handling, spray-booth operation, color formulation, and paint safety is desirable.

    2. Experience

    5 years of experience as a Paint Technician in an authorized passenger vehicle Bodyshop.Hands-on experience with OEM-specified paint systems, multi-layer coatings, color matching, paint-booth operations, paint-material control, final paint inspection, defect correction, and repair-process documentation is desirable.Experience in coordinating EV/PHEV temperature & bake time restrictions with Bodyshop controller is preferred.

    3. Key Responsibilities

    A. Job Review and Paint-Process Preparation
    • Review the allocated repair order, vehicle color code, repair-stage status, and planned delivery schedule before commencing work.
    • Confirm that the panel is ready for painting in accordance with the applicable repair-stage requirements.
    • Promptly report any issues affecting paint quality, rework, material availability, booth scheduling, or job completion to the Bodyshop Controller.
    B. Surface Preparation and Masking
    • Assess repaired panels and adjacent areas to determine surface-preparation requirements before refinishing.
    • Mask and protect non-painted parts and other vulnerable areas to prevent overspray and contamination.
    • Follow proper surface preparation practices to prevent contamination and minimize paint defects.
    C. Color Matching and Paint Mixing
    • Verify the vehicle’s colour information and follow approved colour-formulation processes.
    • Use the approved color swatch set for accurate paint identification, matching, and mixing.
    • Use approved color formulas and test spray cards for accurate color matching under suitable lighting.
    • Ensure correct formula selection and material usage to minimize paint wastages.
    D. Spray-Booth Operation and Paint Application
    • Verify paint-booth readiness and report any equipment issues affecting paint quality or safety.
    • Maintain the paint booth, paint room, equipment, and work area in a clean, organized, and safe condition.
    E. EV/PHEV Refinishing Controls
    • Verify manufacturer-approved refinishing and curing-temperature requirements before moving (EV/PHEV or hybrid) vehicles into the paint booth.
    • Coordinate with the Bodyshop Controller to confirm painting suitability for vehicles with (battery or underbody damage or other technical restrictions).
    F. Curing, Finish Correction and Paint Quality Inspection
    • Perform polishing, buffing, and detailing to correct minor paint-finish imperfections.
    • Conduct final paint-quality inspection under appropriate lighting before the vehicle progresses to the next Process.
    • Report color mismatches, paint defects, material inconsistencies, or equipment issues, and rework risks to the Bodyshop Controller.
    G. Documentation, Materials, Equipment and Safety
    • Document paint material usage, color code, formula, variant, mix quantity and final inspection result through the designated process.
    • Monitor paint and consumable usage against the repair order and number of panels painted.
    • Report tool and equipment calibration, maintenance, along with material requirements, to ensure timely job completion.
    • Adhere to prescribed PPE, 5S, fire safety, chemical handling, and workplace safety requirements during painting operations.
    • Coordinate with the Bodyshop Controller and relevant workshop teams to ensure smooth repair flow and delivery readiness.

    4. Key Performance Indicators (KPIs)

    Finish Quality
    • Paint rework percentage, including internal and external rework
    Material consumption
    • Per Panel Consumption – Paint and Non-Paint
    • Monthly Paint Booth fuel consumption
    Process, Safety and Compliance
    • Paint Booth Filter replacement compliance

    5. Key Competencies

    Ability to interpret applicable OEM or paint-system technical data sheets, color formulas, repair-method requirements, cure limits, and refinish bulletins.Surface preparation, sanding, filling, primer application, masking, and contamination-control discipline.Understanding coating systems and process controls.Ability to identify and prevent all kinds of paint defectsSpray-booth environmental-control awareness, including cleanliness, filtration, extraction, compressed-air quality, airflow, and equipment conditionVerify manufacturer-approved refinishing and curing-temperature requirements.Paint-material, consumable-control discipline.safe operation and proper maintenance of all painting tools, equipment as per prescribed standards.Time management, teamwork, attention to detail, and commitment to ongoing technical learning.Brand-value orientations

    Service Technician (body Shop)

    DepartmentAftersales – Body Shop
    Reporting toBodyshop Controller
    Role ImpactMechanical R&I Quality, Reassembly Reliability, Bodyshop Productivity, Safe High-Voltage Work Control, Post-Repair Validation and Customer Satisfaction

    Position Overview

    The Service Technician (Body Shop) is responsible for carrying out mechanical and electrical removal-and-installation (R&I) activities on accident-damaged vehicles to support body repair, structural repair, painting, reassembly, and post-repair validation.

    The role identifies, dismantles, stores, reinstalls, and verifies mechanical, electrical, cooling, steering, suspension, braking, and related vehicle components in accordance with approved repair orders and manufacturer repair information. The Service Technician ensures that removed components and associated fasteners, harnesses, connectors, hoses, clips, modules, and other parts remain protected, traceable, and correctly reinstated through each bodyshop repair stage.

    For EV/PHEV and hybrid vehicles, the role must operate strictly within formal training and authorization boundaries. The Service Technician identifies collision-related concerns involving battery, high-voltage, cooling, electrical, and underbody interfaces; follows approved isolation and protection processes where authorized; and escalates high-voltage, battery, diagnostic, programming, calibration, or other specialist requirements through the approved bodyshop process.

    1. Education

    ITI or Diploma in Automobile Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or related technical discipline.Training or certification in automotive mechanical repair, collision-repair mechanical R&I, and workshop safety is desirable.Training or certification in EV/hybrid collision-related mechanical R&I, high-voltage safety, and battery handling is preferred, where relevant to the assigned work scope.

    2. Experience

    2–5 years of experience as a Service Technician, Mechanical Technician, or Bodyshop Mechanical Technician in an authorized passenger-vehicle workshop or bodyshop.Experience in accident-damage mechanical assessment, dismantling, reassembly, and post-repair functional checks.Exposure to EV/PHEV or hybrid-vehicle collision repair, controlled dismantling, reassembly, and high-voltage safety processes is preferred.

    3. Key Responsibilities

    • Review assigned repair order, work instructions, and available technical information before commencing dismantling or reassembly work.
    • Carry out a pre-repair condition inspection and document the condition of removed components, harness routing, connectors, sensor locations, fluid connections, and visible collision damage through photographs and technician notes.
    • Identify damaged, missing, deformed, heat-affected, contaminated, or non-reusable parts before reassembly. Report additional damage, one-time-use fasteners, special tool requirements, or parts constraints promptly for approval and planning.
    • Remove and disassemble accident-affected mechanical and electrical parts & assemblies.
    • Maintain identification and traceability of removed parts to prevent incorrect installation or loss during body repair and painting stages.
    • Protect exposed connectors, electrical terminals, high-voltage interfaces, open cooling and brake lines from moisture, paint overspray, dirt, heat, corrosion, and physical damage.
    • Inspect harnesses, connectors, retainers, etc. before reassembly. Repair or replace components only through approved methods and escalate any wiring or connector damage to the Bodyshop Controller.
    • Coordinate with Body Technicians and Paint Technicians to ensure structural, panel, paint, and corrosion-protection work is complete before final mechanical reassembly. Prevent damage to newly finished surfaces and protect repaired areas and interior – upholstery and carpets during installation.
    • Recover and refill vehicle air-conditioning refrigerant and battery cooling systems and reassemble all mechanical, electrical, and cooling components properly following body straightening and painting. Torque all fasteners, bleed hydraulic systems, perform wheel alignments and check all fluid levels.
    • Perform functional checks, diagnostic scans, and road tests along with Quality controller/Road tester to ensure zero error codes, fluid leaks, NVH concerns before final quality check.
    • Coordinate handover to Electrical Experts, Diagnostic Experts, or authorized personnel for programming, coding, complex DTC diagnosis, ADAS calibration, high-voltage repair, or technical escalation where the repair requires specialist action.
    • Maintain clean and controlled mechanical R&I work areas, including segregation of removed parts, safe storage of battery-related components, fire safety compliance, and proper storage of refrigerant, coolant, oil, brake fluid, and waste materials.
    • For EV/PHEV, perform high-voltage de-energization and verify zero voltage before body repair work begins.
    • Follow prescribed disconnection and reconnection sequences for low voltage and high voltage electrical interfaces, cooling circuits, restraint-system connectors, electronic modules, sensors, and wiring harnesses and do not force connectors or alter harness routing.
    • Safely lower, store, and reinstall high-voltage battery packs or underbody shields using dedicated battery lifting tables when required.
    • Inspect assigned tools and equipment before using and promptly report unsafe, damaged, uncalibrated, or non-functioning equipment.
    • Maintain safe storage and handling of refrigerant, coolant, oil, brake fluid, and other workshop materials in accordance with applicable dealership procedures.
    • Follow applicable fire safety, PPE, 5S, housekeeping, waste-handling, environmental, workshop-safety, and vehicle-protection requirements.
    • Coordinate professionally with the Bodyshop, Parts and Workshop team members to maintain repair flow.

    4. Key Performance Indicators (KPIs)

    • Turn Around Time for Mechanical work
    • Pending RO Ratio of B&P cars (Daily avg pending to monthly load) – Reason Mech repairs
    • Repeat repair & rework %
    • Body to Mechanical conversion %

    5. Key Competencies

    Mechanical dismantling, removal and installation, component protection, and controlled reassembly skillsAbility to interpret applicable OEM repair manuals, torque specifications, fastener requirements, fluid-service instructions, and technical repair informationParts, fastener, clip, harness, connector, module, hose, and component-identification and traceability disciplineKnowledge of correct harness routing, connector protection, sealing, clips, grommets, grounding, shielding, and component-installation controlsEV/PHEV collision-repair awareness, including high-voltage hazard recognition, isolation boundaries, battery-lifting controls, underbody protection, and escalation requirementsAwareness of battery, high-voltage, electrical, diagnostic, programming, ADAS-calibration, and technical work requiring specialist handoverCooling-system, brake-bleeding, air-conditioning refrigerant, and fluid-service awareness within authorized work scopePost-repair functional check and basic validation discipline, road testing ability for NVH concerns.Safe use and basic care of lifting equipment, battery-handling equipment, workshop tools, fluid-service equipment, and PPEDigital literacy for technician comments, job-card updates, work-status updates, and use of approved workshop applications, tablets, or PCsClear communication of additional damage, parts needs, delays, technical constraints, safety concerns, and handover requirements5S, safety, environmental, fire-prevention, housekeeping, and waste-management disciplineTime management, attention to detail, teamwork, and brand-value orientation

    Parts Manager

    DepartmentAftersales – Parts
    Reporting toGeneral Manager – Aftersales/ Dealer Principal
    Role ImpactParts Availability, Inventory Control, Workshop Support and Parts Department Profitability

    Position Overview

    The Parts Manager is responsible for managing the spare parts and accessories business, including inventory planning, procurement, stock health, counter and wholesale sales, and cost control. Ensure timely parts availability for workshop and retail customers by coordinating with Service and Body Shop teams, forecasting demand, and preventing repair delays. Drive Parts & Accessories sales, profitability, and inventory accuracy, while ensuring proper handling of genuine, warranty, EV/PHEV, and safety-critical components in line with OEM standards and safety requirements.

    1. Education

    Diploma or Graduate qualification in Automobile Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or related discipline preferred.Automotive or supply-chain experience preferred, with hands-on experience in inventory management systems and DMSProfessional certification in Parts/Inventory management is preferred.

    2. Experience

    6–10 years of experience in automotive dealership parts operations.Demonstrated experience in inventory planning, parts ordering, stock control, and team management.Working knowledge of automotive parts, accessories, electronic parts catalogues, ordering processes, goods receipt, storage, returns, and inventory reconciliation.

    3. Key Responsibilities

    A. Parts Business Planning and Commercial Performance
    • Plan parts ordering based on service demand, seasonality, vehicle parc, forthcoming campaigns, and inputs from JSW teams and Service and Body Shop operations.
    • Set and periodically review department sales and profitability targets.
    • Prepare and monitor the parts budget, including purchasing, storage, and inventory-related costs.
    • Monitor parts and accessories sales performance and take appropriate action to support achievement of department targets.
    • Maintain focus on parts availability, inventory health, cost control, and profitability.
    B. Demand Planning, Ordering and Procurement
    • Initiate and consolidate demand planning for Stock Orders and review demand forecasts before submission for OEM review.
    • Identify requirements for new parts and accessories and include them in the ordering plan where appropriate.
    • Monitor Back orders/ Check internal and external stock availability and coordinate stock transfers, where applicable.
    • Proceed with ordering unavailable parts and submit orders to JSW.
    • Generate purchase orders in the Dealer Management System (DMS), as specified in the applicable process.
    • Ensure correct part identification and ordering through the Electronic Parts Catalogue (EPC).
    • Monitor parts-order status and communicate expected receipt timelines for unavailable parts to the relevant Service Advisor.
    • Monitor Vehicle Off Road (VOR)/Emergency Orders ratio
    C. Receiving, Storage and Inventory Accuracy
    • Ensure receipt of shipments is controlled through physical quantity and quality verification, with timely stock updates in the DMS.
    • Ensure spare parts are correctly received, tagged, binned, and made traceable within the inventory-management process.
    • Ensure parts are blocked or allocated to the relevant job card where required, to prevent double allocation.
    • Conduct regular physical inventory checks, investigate stock discrepancies, and ensure necessary reconciliation action is taken.
    • Monitor stock levels, stock holding days, inventory turnover, slow-moving inventory, and obsolete stock.
    • Take corrective action to reduce inventory ageing, overstocking, and obsolete-stock exposure.
    • Ensure physical storage conditions are appropriate for genuine parts, accessories, warranty items, and shelf-life items.
    D. Workshop, Service and Body Shop Support
    • Ensure timely issue of parts for Service and Body Shop repair jobs.
    • Coordinate with the Service Manager and Body Shop Manager to identify, monitor, and clear pending jobs caused by parts non-availability.
    • Support timely picking of issued parts to the technician through the Parts picker.
    • Maintain clear and regular coordination with Service and Body Shop teams to forecast demand and minimize repair delays caused by parts shortages.
    • Review parts-availability issues that affect vehicle turnaround time and support resolution through ordering, stock checks, transfers, or expected-receipt communication.
    E. Returns & Process Compliance

    • Ensure genuine parts; accessories are handled in line with applicable brand guidelines.
    • Maintain compliance with parts-ordering procedures, return processes, and inventory-control practices.
    F. EV/PHEV Parts and Team Management
    • Ensure that EV/PHEV components are identified, stored, and issued in accordance with approved safety guidelines and brand standards.
    • Provide operational guidance, performance monitoring, and coaching to the Parts Executive and other approved Parts-team members.
    • Promote process discipline, stock accuracy, safety awareness, cross-functional coordination, and customer service orientation within the Parts team.

    • Dead/Obsolete Stock ratio
    • VOR order ratio

    • Parts-order turnaround time
    • Timeliness of parts issue and delivery for repair jobs

    Parts Executive

    DepartmentAfter Sales – Parts
    Reporting toParts Manager
    Role ImpactParts Availability, Counter Service Efficiency, Correct Parts Supply, Accurate Parts Receipting & Binning, Stock Accuracy, Inventory Health, Workshop Productivity, and Safe Parts Handling

    Position Overview

    The Parts Executive is responsible for day-to-day parts counter and store operations, including (Parts identification, receipt verification, binning, storage, picking, and issue) Ensure FIFO and 5S implementation, maintain accurate inventory records traceability between physical parts movement and system transactions & identify and prepare report slow-moving, damaged, or obsolete stock.

    1. Education

    ITI, Diploma, or; or Graduate in any field.Training in automotive parts operations, EPC/DMS use, warehouse management, inventory control, safe material handling, and EV/PHEV parts awareness, storage requirements are desirable.

    3 years of experience in automotive spare parts counter operations, inventory handling, or parts store management in an authorized passenger vehicle dealership.3 years in parts/inventory handling, automotive preferred to indent the Automotive component.Basic proficiency in MS Excel, with experience in using Electronic Parts Catalogues (EPC) and Dealer Management Systems (DMS) preferred

    • Look up exact part numbers in the Electronic Parts Catalogue (EPC) using applicable Vehicle Identification number (VIN). Clarify incomplete requirements with the requester, and refer to any queries, replacement/substitute parts, or substitutions to the Parts Manager before issuing against RO in DMS.

    • Maintain accurate bin locations and apply FIFO stock rotation to ensure error-free picking, verification, and shelf-life control.
    • Monitor inventory levels of fast-moving service parts and consumables and submit replenishment requisitions to the Parts Manager.

    • Handle customer and counter parts inquiries with clear pricing, availability, and delivery updates. Verify returned parts against the original transaction and check their quantity, condition, packaging, and identification before further processing, if authorized by the PM.
    • Coordinate with technicians and Service Advisors regarding backorder or pending parts, providing expected arrival dates.
    • Follow safe handling and storage procedures for sensitive electronic modules, sensors, batteries, and high-voltage parts.
    • Keep the parts counter, store racks, and receiving area clean, organized, and compliant with 5S standards.

    • WIP due to PNA Cases

    • Completion of scheduled cycle counts and inventory checks.
    • Compliance with storage, handling, labelling, FIFO, and safety requirements during Brand Standard Audits.

    Accurate automotive parts identification using EPC, VIN information.Working knowledge of genuine spare parts, lubricants, consumables, and fast-moving maintenance items.Proficiency in approved DMS and parts-transaction workflows, subject to assigned access.Accurate receiving, picking, binning, issue, reservation, and stock-recording skills.Understanding repair-order and transaction documentation discipline.Inventory-counting, reconciliation support, and discrepancy-identification skills.Knowledge of storage and preservation requirements for sensitive and safety-critical parts.Awareness of EV/PHEV parts-handling risks, role boundaries, and escalation requirements.Clear communication with technicians, Service Advisors, bodyshop teams, customers, and the Parts Manager.Attention to detail, integrity in stock handling, follow-up discipline, and adherence to approved processes.

    CRM Service

    DepartmentAftersales – Customer Relations
    Reporting toGM – Aftersales/ Dealer Principal
    Role ImpactCustomer Satisfaction, Service Retention, Customer Communication and Complaint Resolution

    Position Overview

    The CRM Service role leads the dealership’s Aftersales customer-relations activities across service reminders, appointment support, post-service follow-up, customer feedback, complaint management, and retention support. The role is responsible for ensuring that customer interactions are timely, accurately recorded, professionally handled, and coordinated with Service and Bodyshop teams.

    The role monitors customer-contact performance, appointment outcomes, post-service feedback, complaint trends, and lost-customer data to help improve customer experience and service retention. It works with the Service Manager, Bodyshop Manager, Service Advisors, and CRM team to track customer concerns through resolution, communicate progress to customers, and support action plans that reduce recurrence of common concerns.

    1. Education

    Graduate in any discipline, preferably Business-related.Certification in CRM courses preferred.

    2. Experience

    5+ years of experience in customer relations, service operations, tele-calling, or related customer-contact roles.Experience in handling CRM activities with proven track record in improving NPS, CSI ranking, customer retention, and service quality performance for a business entity.

    3. Key Responsibilities

    A. Customer Contact, Reminders and Appointment Management
    • Plan and monitor service reminders, welcome calls, appointment-related calls, and post-service follow-up activities.
    • Set monthly contact and appointment-performance expectations for Customer Relationship Executives (CREs), including customer contact, appointment scheduling, appointment confirmation, appointment conversion, and customer visits against appointments.
    • Review daily calling lists, including service-due customers, missed appointments, rescheduled appointments, no-show-up cases, and non-contactable customers.
    • Monitor the status of appointments and ensure appropriate customer communication for appointment reminders, scheduling, and follow-up.
    • Support the CRM team in identifying customer requirements related to appointment slots and pick-up/drop-off requirements, as per Brand SOP.
    • Review no-show trends and coordinate appropriate follow-up to support customer re-engagement.
    B. Post-Service Follow-up and Customer Feedback
    • Ensure timely completion of post-service follow-up (PSFU) activities and accurate documentation of customer feedback.
    • Monitor the quality of customer calls, including professional communication, query handling, follow-up discipline, and documentation of call outcomes.
    • Track customer satisfaction feedback, including dissatisfied customer responses, and ensure appropriate follow-up is initiated.
    • Ensure customer satisfaction ratings, feedback, and verbatim reasons for dissatisfaction are captured appropriately in the relevant system.
    • Share customer feedback trends and recurring concerns with Service and Bodyshop teams to support service-experience improvement.
    C. Customer Complaint and Case Management
    • Act as a customer-contact point for Aftersales concerns and grievances in accordance with the documented process.
    • Review customer cases, conduct resolution follow-up, and ensure customer concerns are documented and tracked until closure.
    • Coordinate with the Service Manager, Bodyshop Manager, Service Advisors, and relevant teams to define and monitor actions for customer-concern resolution.
    • Contact dissatisfied customers to understand the concern, capture relevant details, and communicate progress on the resolution.
    • Monitor complaint resolution timelines, case status, and unresolved cases; follow up with the responsible teams for timely closure.
    • Escalate repeat repairs, serious customer concerns, and unresolved cases to the GM – Aftersales.
    • Support customer discussions with the Service Manager, where required, to communicate the proposed resolution and provide satisfactory closure.
    • Review and manage the closure process for customer cases, including resolution calls, customer satisfaction notes, and case-status updates in the relevant CRM process.
    • Conduct root-cause analysis of customer complaints, using structured problem-solving tools such as 5-Why analysis and Fishbone diagrams, in coordination with Service and Bodyshop teams, to identify underlying causes and support corrective and preventive actions.
    • Support action planning with Service and Bodyshop teams to address recurring complaints and reduce repetition of customer concerns.
    D. Service Retention and Lost-Customer Follow-up
    • Review customers who have stopped visiting the dealership for service and identify opportunities for re-engagement.
    • Plan and monitor retention activities for customers identified as lost in the dealership’s customer data.
    • Track customer-contact rate, appointment conversion, customer visit ratio, and retention-related outcomes to identify areas requiring follow-up or improvement.
    • Share missed-visit, retention, and customer-contact trends with Service and Bodyshop teams for coordinated action.
    E. CRM Data Quality and Customer Information Management
    • Ensure customer details, contact preferences, call records, appointment outcomes, feedback, and follow-up status are updated accurately in the DMS and applicable CRM process.
    • Monitor CRM-team compliance with timely and accurate updates of customer interactions and case records.
    • Review data-quality issues, incomplete records, and inaccurate call outcomes, and ensure corrective action is taken.
    • Ensure customer information is handled carefully and support practices that prevent unauthorized customer data disclosure or leakage.
    F. Team Leadership and Capability Support
    • Guide, monitor, and coach CREs on communication quality (by way of call calibration), customer handling, follow-up discipline, appointment management, feedback capture, and record updating.
    • Review individual and team performance on agreed KPIs.
    • Identify capability gaps within the CRM team and arrange or recommend appropriate coaching and training support.
    • Maintain a customer-focused, solution-oriented, professional, and collaborative work environment in CRM teams.
    G. Aftersales Process and EV/PHEV Customer Support
    • Maintain working knowledge of Aftersales service processes, service terms and conditions, customer-contact requirements, and customer-feedback processes.
    • Maintain basic knowledge of EV/PHEV maintenance and service requirements to guide the CRM team in handling customer queries professionally.
    • Coordinate with relevant Aftersales teams when customer queries require operational or technical clarification.

    4. Key Performance Indicators (KPIs)

    Customer Experience and Complaint Management
    • Customer Satisfaction Index (CSI) / Net Promoter Score (NPS)
    • Complaints per thousand vehicles (CPTV)
    • Track and improve complaint resolution time and complaint closure rate (% complaints resolved)
    Customer Contact and Retention
    • Service-reminder completion rate
    • Post-service follow-up completion rate
    • Customer contact percentage
    • Appointment-scheduling percentage
    • Appointment-confirmation percentage
    • Appointment-conversion percentage
    • Customer visit ratio against appointments
    • Missed appointment and no-show follow-up status
    • Customer-retention and lost-customer re-engagement ratio

    5. Key Competencies

    Customer relations and Aftersales service-process knowledgeClear verbal and written communicationProfessional telephone etiquetteActive listening, empathy, and customer handlingComplaint handling, resolution follow-up, and customer reassuranceCustomer-feedback analysis and trend identificationFollow-up planning, appointment tracking, and pipeline managementTeam guidance, coaching, and performance monitoringCross-functional coordination with Service and Bodyshop teamsCRM, DMS, and customer-record managementData accuracy, documentation discipline, and attention to detailCustomer-information confidentiality and data-handling awarenessCalm, solution-oriented problem solvingBrand-value orientationBasic awareness of EV/PHEV service requirements and related customer expectations

    CRE Service

    DepartmentAftersales – Customer Relations
    Reporting toCRM Service
    Role ImpactService Appointments, Customer Follow-up, Customer Data Accuracy and Service-Reception Experience

    Position Overview

    The Customer Relationship Executive (CRE) – Service supports the Aftersales customer journey through service-due reminders, appointment scheduling, post-service follow-up, feedback capture, and accurate customer-record maintenance. The role serves as an important customer-contact point before, during, and after a service visit.

    The CRE Service is responsible for making timely customer contact, recording outcomes accurately, coordinating relevant appointment and visit information with Aftersales teams, and ensuring customer concerns are captured and escalated through the defined process. The role must provide courteous, clear, and professional support while referring technical, warranty, safety, and other specialized queries to the appropriate trained team member.

    1. Education

    Graduate in any discipline.

    2. Experience

    2+ years of experience in customer service, tele-calling, or a dealership service role.Experience of service-due reminder calls and post-service follow-up calls in an automotive dealership is preferred.Experience in customer calling, appointment handling, customer data updates, feedback capture, and customer-facing coordination.

    3. Key Responsibilities

    A. Customer Data and Calling-List Management
    • Maintain accurate customer data required for service-due reminders, appointment calls, welcome calls, and post-service follow-up activities.
    • Review assigned calling lists and priorities for timely outreach in line with scheduled customer-contact requirements.
    • Update customer contact details, customer calling preferences, call outcomes, and relevant interaction status in the Dealer Management System (DMS).
    • Record unsuccessful contact attempts, incorrect contact details, customer callback requests, and other call outcomes accurately.
    • Follow prescribed, call scripts where applicable, data-entry requirements, privacy rules, and brand service standards.
    B. Service-Due Reminders and Appointment Scheduling
    • Contact customers when their vehicle service is due (as per standard service schedules), explain the purpose of the service reminder, and offer suitable available appointment slots.
    • Obtain relevant appointment information from customers, including preferred date, time, location, and pick-up/drop-off requirements where applicable.
    • Check available service and pick-up/drop-off slots through the standard process before confirming customer appointments.
    • Confirm service appointments with customers and record appointment details accurately in the applicable system.
    • Conduct appointment confirmation calls before scheduled appointments, as required by the defined process.
    • Follow up on missed appointments and no-show cases, understand the reason where possible, and support rescheduling.
    • Communicate with confirmed appointments and visit information to the relevant Service Advisors and Parts team.
    • Respond to incoming service-related calls, understand the customer’s request, and either schedule the appointment or route the request to the appropriate team member.
    • Return missed customer calls within the defined turnaround time under the documented process.
    C. Welcome Calls and Customer Onboarding Support
    • Conduct welcome calls where service introduction has not been completed, in accordance with the documented process.
    • Communicate the relevant information during welcome calls, including the importance of scheduled maintenance, standard warranty and the availability of Aftersales support.
    • Update welcome-call completion, non-contact, and callback status accurately in the relevant system.
    • Escalate adverse feedback or concerns identified during welcome calls to the CRM Service.
    D. Post-Service Follow-up and Feedback Capture
    • Conduct post-service follow-up calls and capture customer feedback within the standard process.
    • Record customer satisfaction ratings against the required post-service feedback attributes.
    • Capture the customer’s stated reason or verbatim feedback when dissatisfaction is expressed.
    • Identify unresolved concerns, repeat concerns, or negative feedback and flag them promptly to CRM Service for further action.
    • Update post-service follow-up status, feedback details, and call outcomes accurately in the applicable system.
    E. Customer Concern Handling and Escalation
    • Listen carefully to customer queries and concerns, acknowledge them professionally, and record the relevant details accurately.
    • Coordinate with the relevant Aftersales team for updates on customer concerns reported in the vehicle where required.
    • Refer technical, warranty, repair-quality, safety, or EV/PHEV-related questions to trained and authorized team members rather than providing unsupported guidance.
    • Follow up on promised customer callbacks and provide updates through the appropriate process.
    • Escalate customer concerns in accordance with the defined CRM and Aftersales escalation process.
    F. EV/PHEV Customer-Query Routing and Process Compliance
    • Maintain basic awareness of EV/PHEV-related service and charging queries to identify the nature of customer requests and route them correctly.
    • Do not provide technical, diagnostic, warranty, or safety advice beyond the CRE Service role defined scope.
    • Handle customer information responsibly and maintain confidentiality in all customer-contact, record-update, and follow-up activities.

    4. Key Performance Indicators (KPIs)

    • Welcome-call completion status, where assigned
    • Post-service follow-up completion rate

    • Appointment visit rate
    • No-Show and missed-appointment follow-up
    • Non-contactable Ratio

    • Concerns Per Thousand Vehicles (CPTV)

    Polite telephone and face-to-face communicationProfessional customer-service orientation and patienceActive listening and accurate feedback captureService appointment scheduling and follow-up-process knowledgeCustomer-data accuracy and system-entry disciplineDMS and customer-record management skillsTime management, call planning, and task prioritizationFollow-through on committed customer callbacksCoordination with Service Advisors, Parts, CRM, and relevant Aftersales teamsCustomer-concern identification and timely escalationBasic understanding of Aftersales service processesBasic awareness of EV/PHEV customer queries and correct routing requirementsCustomer-information confidentiality and privacy awarenessBrand-value orientation

    Service Marketing Executive

    DepartmentAfter Sales
    Reporting toCustomer Relations Manager (CRM)
    Role ImpactService Workshop Footfall, Customer Retention & Win-Back, VAS Campaign Revenue & Brand Engagement

    Position Overview

    The Service Marketing Executive is responsible for supporting the planning, execution, coordination, tracking, and review of Aftersales marketing campaigns and customer engagement initiatives.

    The role works with Aftersales team members, dealership marketing support, and other relevant teams to promote approved service offerings, improve workshop footfall, encourage timely service appointments, reactivate lost customers, and support customer retention.

    The role is responsible for ensuring that campaigns are thoughtfully planned, approved, accurately targeted, communicated through approved channels, tracked through to customer response and workshop conversion, and reviewed for learning and improvement. The role must ensure that customer communications, campaign content, offers, eligibility conditions, promotional material, and data use comply with OEM, dealership, customer-consent, and brand requirements.

    The Service Marketing Executive does not independently approve commercial offers, campaign budgets with this authority remaining with GM Service/Business Head.

    1. Education

    Graduate or bachelor’s degree in marketing, Business Administration, Mass Communication, or related field.Certification or training in digital marketing, CRM campaign management, customer-lifecycle management, data analytics, or automotive service marketing is desirable.Training in customer communication, brand-guideline compliance, customer-data confidentiality, or campaign analytics is desirable.

    2. Experience

    2–4 years of experience in service marketing, CRM campaign execution, customer retention, customer outreach, digital campaign coordination, or a related customer engagement role. Experience in executing customer outreach campaigns, service-camp promotions, appointment-generation initiatives, or customer reactivation programs is desirable.Experience in an automotive dealership, customer-lifecycle and retail service environment, or another structured customer-marketing function is desirable.Exposure to CRM/DMS data, customer segmentation, campaign reporting, bulk-messaging platforms, or digital communication channels is desirable.

    3. Key Responsibilities

    • Prepare a monthly or periodic campaign plan in line with approved business priorities, seasonality with target segment, offer, channel, budget, booking target, revenue target, and review date.
    • Define the purpose of each proposed campaign, such as service-due conversion, customer retention, or customer education along with planned campaign timelines, workshop coordination, and post campaign review requirements.
    • Maintain a clear campaign brief covering objectives, audience, value proposition, communication, booking process, and success measures.
    • Obtain required approval before releasing customer offers, campaign content, discounts, event material, or campaign communication
    • Ensure campaign content states applicable offer terms, validity period, eligibility criteria, appointment requirements, and customer contact/booking mode while maintaining appropriate records.
    • Use customer information only through approved systems, approved access rights, and approved customer-contact processes with customer consent and confidentiality and brand requirements.
    • Work with CRM teams to identify appropriate customer segments for approved Aftersales campaigns using available CRM/DMS information, such as customers due for service, Inactive customers etc.
    • Before launch, coordinate with Service Advisors, Parts, Bodyshop, and Workshop teams to confirm operational readiness for campaign offers and ensure leads are handled through the approved booking process within available workshop capacity.
    • Coordinate with the tele-calling team to align approved campaign scripts, offer conditions, eligibility, campaign dates, and appointment-booking prompts, and ensure campaign responses are recorded accurately.
    • Work with dealership marketing and design teams to prepare and place approved campaign collaterals, such as digital banners, leaflets, and customer lounge standees.
    • Manage digital outreach via WhatsApp Business API, SMS broadcasts, email marketing, and social media platforms adhering to OEM brand guidelines.
    • Organize corporate service tie-ups, residential community camps, and EV customer educational clinics to expand the dealership customer base.
    • Track each campaign from launch through response, leads, bookings, workshop visits, and billing, monitoring conversion at every stage and measuring ROI.
    • Monitor competitor aftersales promotions, pricing messages, service-camp activity, and observable market practices, and report factual observations, providing actionable insights for service marketing strategies.
    • Maintain accurate campaign records covering objective, target segment, channel, dates, responses, leads, appointments, visits, billed value, spend, and outcome conversion, learning, and next action.

    4. Key Performance Indicators (KPIs)

    Campaign Planning and Execution
    • Percentage of actual approved campaigns launched vs planned.
    Footfall Growth & Revenue
    • Increase in workshop thruput and revenue generated from marketing campaigns (Revenue with vs without campaigns)
    • Success rate in dormant and lost customer reactivation / win-back campaigns
    • Growth in Value Added Service enquiries, booking, conversions, and revenue contributions.
    • Accurate campaign targeting and reduced duplicate, ineligible, or invalid outreach.
    Campaign Efficiency & ROI
    • Campaign-generated Lead to Appointment; Appointment to actual workshop visit, Visit to Billing value conversion
    • Campaign lead-to-booking conversion rate across digital and tele-calling channels
    • % Lost-customer reactivation rate: (% of targeted lost customers who return for a paid workshop visit within XX days of the campaign)
    • Cost per workshop lead and overall marketing campaign Return on Investment (ROI)
    • Accuracy of campaign targeting, including % reduction in non-contactable customers.
    • 4. Service Reminder
    • Service Retention
    • Warranty, Insurance Marketing
    • Post Service Feedback, Grievance Redressal
    • ROI Tracking
