    Service Reception Co-Ordinator

    DepartmentAftersales – CRM Service
    Reporting toCRM Service
    Role ImpactCustomer Reception Experience, Workshop Arrival Flow, Service Advisor Allocation, Customer Waiting-Time Management, Lounge Readiness, and Customer Satisfaction

    Position Overview

    The Service Reception Co-Ordinator is responsible for managing the customer’s reception and waiting experience when they arrive at the workshop for a scheduled appointment or as a walk-in customer.

    The role serves as the primary coordination point between the arriving customer, Service Advisor, Service CRE, reception and lounge support/ housekeeping personnel, and other relevant Aftersales teams. The Service Reception Co-Ordinator ensures that customers are welcomed professionally, their workshop arrival and appointment status are appropriately verified with courtesy, and they are handed over to an available Service Advisor in a timely and orderly manner.

    The role maintains visibility of customer queues, appointment status, Service Advisor availability, and job-card-opening progress through the DMS. It also ensures that customers waiting in the lounge receive clear guidance, reasonable comfort, and timely updates where a delay occurs. The role must not diagnose vehicles, create technical estimates, commit repair completion times, approve job cards, or resolve technical complaints independently; such matters remain with the authorized Service Advisor, Service Manager, CRM Service, or other designated role.

    1. Education

    Graduate, diploma holder, or equivalent qualification in Hospitality, Business Administration, Customer Service, Public Relations, or another relevant discipline.Training in front-office operations, customer hospitality, communication, business etiquette, or customer service handling is desirable.

    2. Experience

    1–3 years of experience in a customer-facing reception, front-office, hospitality, customer-service, or dealership support role.Experience in customer greeting, customer waiting-area coordination, or call handling is desirable.Experience in an automotive dealership, automotive service facility, premium retail, hospitality, or another structured customer service environment is preferred.Exposure to customer data handling, appointment systems, CRM/DMS systems, or service-reception processes is desirable.

    3. Key Responsibilities

    A. Reception Readiness and Daily Preparation
    • Prepare the service-reception and customer-lounge area before the start of customer operations.
    • Confirm that the reception desk, customer appointment display, appointment information, and relevant reception supplies are available and presentable.
    • Review the day’s appointment list, expected customer arrivals, Service Advisor allocation status, and relevant reception instructions.
    • Maintain visibility of Service Advisor availability, Appointment customer lists, overall job-card-opening progress.
    • Ensure the reception, lounge area and customer-facing material are clean, orderly, presentable, and maintained in accordance with applicable housekeeping and 5S standards in coordination with housekeeping personnel.
    B. Customer Greeting and Arrival Support
    • Coordinate with the security gate, valet for smooth customer movement from workshop entry to reception and onward to the Service Advisor
    • Greet every arriving customer promptly, courteously, and professionally at the reception area.
    • Guide the customer through the next stage of the workshop-arrival process and advise them of the expected Service Advisor interaction.
    • Support appointments with customers and walk-in customers in accordance with the approved reception process.
    • Customer details are kept ready in the DMS beforehand including appointment status, vehicle registration details, visit type, and Service Advisor allocation status.
    • Guide customers to the lounge or other designated waiting area while they wait for Service Advisor allocation or engagement.
    • Provide additional assistance to customers who may require support due to age, mobility needs, children accompanying them, language requirements, or other observable customer-comfort requirements.
    • Treat all customers with courtesy, impartiality, discretion, and professional respect.
    C. Appointment Preparation and Service Advisor Allocation
    • Look over the day's appointments in the DMS ahead of time, then greet those customers by name when they arrive.
    • Coordinate Service Advisor allocation for customers with appointments, where the originally allocated Service Advisor is unavailable, coordinate allocation of an alternate available Service Advisor on priority with CRM. Meanwhile, guide the customer to the Customer lounge.
    • Coordinate allocation of walk-in customers to an available Service Advisor based on the applicable allocation priority and available capacity.
    • Avoid committing a customer to a specific repair scope, estimate, technical outcome, repair completion time, or job-card decision; refer such matters to the assigned Service Advisor.
    • Escalate capacity constraints, prolonged waiting times, Service Advisor non-availability, or repeated allocation concerns to CRM Service or the Service Manager.
    D. Customer Lounge Experience and Waiting-Time Management
    • Escort or guide customers to the designated customer lounge after reception. Brief customers on the available lounge facilities.
    • Maintain awareness of customer waiting time during workshop intake, Service Advisor allocation, job-card opening, and vehicle delivery.
    • Provide timely, courteous, and accurate updates when the assigned Service Advisor is delayed or when the customer needs to continue waiting.
    • Coordinate with the relevant team if a customer requires assistance related to refreshments, lounge comfort, accessories enquiry, local transit, or other non-technical customer-service requirements.
    • Maintain a calm, attentive, and orderly reception environment, particularly during peak arrival and delivery periods.
    E. Telephone, Enquiry, and Customer Communication Support
    • Answer incoming reception calls professionally and identify the nature of the caller’s enquiry.
    • Provide approved information within the role of authority or direct the caller to the appropriate department.
    • Route appointment, service-status, technical, billing, warranty, complaint, parts, and other specialized enquiries to the appropriate authorized person or team.
    • Record or communicate missed-call, callback, customer-contact, or enquiry details in accordance with the approved process where this responsibility is assigned.
    F. Customer Concern Identification and Escalation
    • Listen attentively when a customer raises a concern, request, dissatisfaction, or complaint at the reception point.
    • Acknowledge the customer’s concern respectfully without making unsupported commitments or assigning faults.
    • Promptly inform the CRM Service, Service Manager, assigned Service Advisor, or other designated authority based on the nature of the concern.
    • Escalate immediately any concern involving customer safety, aggressive behavior, serious dissatisfaction, repeated service concerns, or an issue requiring management attention.
    G. Records, Process Discipline, and Coordination
    • Maintain accurate records, where assigned, of customer arrival, waiting status, Service Advisor allocation, callback needs, delay reasons, and escalated concerns through the approved system or record format.
    • Coordinate professionally with Service Advisors, CRM Service, Service CRE, Service Manager, gate/security staff, drivers, housekeeping, pantry personnel, and other relevant teams.
    • Follow dealership requirements for grooming, attendance, punctuality, customer data confidentiality, workplace conduct, safety, housekeeping, and brand presentation.

    4. Key Performance Indicators (KPIs)

    Reception Efficiency and Customer Flow
    • Customer waiting time from arrival to Service Advisor engagement.
    Customer Experience and Hospitality
    • Customer feedback on reception welcome, courtesy, clarity of communication, lounge support, and overall arrival experience.

    5. Key Competencies

    Interpersonal & Communication CompetenciesActive Listening and EmpathyProfessional, warm, and clear verbal communication.Strong customer service orientation, hospitality etiquette, and professional grooming.Ability to welcome and guide customers confidently in a busy service environment.Active listening, empathy, composure, and tact while handling customer concerns.Ability to coordinate multiple arriving customers/ stakeholders.Basic digital proficiency and ability to use approved CRM, DMS, appointment, queue management, or reception systems.Ability to interpret appointment status, customer-arrival information, Service Advisor availability, and allocation of information presented in approved systems.Accurate recordkeeping and attention to detail.Understanding role boundaries and timely escalation of technical, commercial, warranty, billing, or complaint matters.Customer data confidentiality and responsible information handling.Teamwork and effective coordination with Service Advisors, CRM Service, CRE Service, gate/security staff, housekeeping, pantry teams, and other support functions.Housekeeping, 5S, lounge-readiness, and customer-comfort awareness.Ability to remain calm, courteous, organized, and responsive during peak workshop-arrival periods.

    Pick & Drop Driver

    DepartmentAfter Sales
    Reporting toCustomer Relations Manager / CRM Service
    Role ImpactSafe Vehicle Movement, On-Time Pickup/Drop Customer Courtesy & Convenience, Professional Vehicle Handover & Customer Satisfaction

    Position Overview

    The Pick & Drop Driver is responsible for the safe, timely, and professional pickup and delivery of customer vehicles for service and repairs. The role ensures safe vehicle handling, punctual service, and courteous customer interaction. The Driver is also responsible for vehicle handover at the customer’s premises, explaining completed work and relevant documents.

    1. Education

    Minimum 12th pass with a valid 4-wheeler driving license appropriate to the vehicles driven and assigned duties.Basic training in safe driving practices, customer service, road safety, vehicle handover, or EV/PHEV handling awareness is desirable.

    2. Experience

    2 to 5 years of professional driving experience, with good experience driving (Manual, automatic, hybrid & Electric) modern passenger cars.Clean driving record with zero accidents or traffic violations, subject to verification.Experience in customer pickup and drop, workshop parking, dealership driving duties, or dealership vehicle movement is preferred.Familiarity with local routes, traffic conditions, and digital navigation tools is an advantage.

    3. Key Responsibilities

    • Collect and return customer vehicles safely and punctually committed according to customer by front office teams. Install/remove protection covers as per brand guidelines during pick-up and drop in presence of customer.
    • Conduct walkaround inspections to note any visible damage or warning indicators, and verify seating, mirrors, and cabin controls before moving the vehicle. Handle customer vehicles, keys, and belongings carefully and report visible damage promptly at the time of pick-up.
    • Check fuel and battery-charge levels before pickup, inform the customer of low levels, and coordinate with the Service Advisor where available range or vehicle warnings may affect safe transport.
    • Present a well-groomed appearance and carry dealership identification during customer visits and always maintain courteous communication and inform the coordinating team of delays or changes affecting pickup or delivery.
    • Show the customer around the serviced vehicle at delivery and offer a joint test drive where required and authorized.
    • Present the vehicle clean and ready for handover, attending to minor spot-cleaning needs at the customer’s premises where required.
    • Hand over the invoice and relevant documents, referring technical explanations and billing queries to the Service Advisor.
    • Collect authorized card payments through credit card swiping machine, where available, and report payment status to the responsible team.
    • Obtain customer feedback and promptly communicate dissatisfaction or unresolved concerns to the Service Advisor or CRM team.
    • Confirm completed delivery to the coordinating team and maintain the required trip, payment, and handover records.
    • Support loaner-car return checks when assigned and report visible damage or discrepancies.
    • Follow traffic rules, dealership security requirements, and approved EV/PHEV driving and handling instructions.
    • Avoid unauthorized commitments to repairs, charges, or delivery.

    4. Key Performance Indicators (KPIs)

    Punctuality & Service
    • On-time customer pickup and drop delivery as per schedule
    Customer Service & Payment Accountability
    • Positive customer feedback on courtesy, vehicle presentation, and handover experience.

    5. Key Competencies

    Safe and smooth driving of assigned passenger vehicles.Knowledge of local routes, traffic rules, and navigation tools.Professional customer etiquette and presentable appearance.Careful vehicle handling, condition observation, and key custody.Clear communication and courteous vehicle presentation.Basic EV/PHEV driving and safety awareness.Integrity, confidentiality, punctuality, and recordkeeping discipline.Clear communication and courteous presentation of the serviced vehicle at customer handoverAbility to remain calm, alert, punctual, and safety focused on traffic conditionsIntegrity and honesty in handling customer payments, documents, keys, and belongings

    Service Cashier

    DepartmentAfter Sales
    Reporting toCFO/ Account & Finance Head
    Role ImpactBilling Accuracy, Secure Payment Collection, Payment Reconciliation, Gate Pass Release & Customer Satisfaction

    Position Overview

    The Service Cashier is responsible for preparing accurate service and bodyshop customer invoices, collecting, recording payments, and issuing payment receipts and gate passes for after-sales service and repairs as per dealership financial procedures. The role ensures that repair bills are accurate, payments are collected through approved modes, daily cash and digital collections are reconciled, and good customers experience through smooth checkout process.

    The role ensures financial accuracy, revenue collection, document control, secured payment handling and timely reconciliation

    1. Education

    Graduate in Commerce, Accounting, Finance, Business Administration (BCom/BBA), or related field.Training in billing controls, GST, digital payments, accounting procedures and customer handling is desirable

    2. Experience

    1 to 3 years of experience as a Cashier, Billing Executive, or Accounts Assistant in an automotive dealership or retail counter.Familiarity with Dealer Management Systems (DMS), POS card machines, UPI payments, and account reconciliation is desired.

    3. Key Responsibilities

    • Confirm the correct customer, vehicle registration number, job card reference, advisor, service type, and billing status before generating an invoice.
    • Check that labour, parts, consumables, sublet work, discounts, taxes, and approved charges match the job card and supporting documents.
    • Raise any billing mismatch, missing approval, duplicate line item, incorrect tax detail, or system concern with the responsible advisor or Accounts team before payment collection.
    • Generate final service and bodyshop invoices from approved job cards in the Dealer Management System (DMS), verifying labour charges, parts, discounts, and GST.
    • Collect payments from customers through approved digital modes (credit/debit cards, UPI, net banking) and cash, issuing official receipts immediately.
    • Handle cash securely, count it in the customer presence where appropriate, and store it only in the authorized cash drawer or safe.
    • Process insurance cashless claim settlement documents, calculating customer liability, deductibles, salvage, and depreciation on an accurate basis for the Insurance delivery order.
    • Explain invoice line items, parts charges, labour costs, and taxes clearly and politely to customers during payment settlement.
    • Generate and release authorized digital or printed gate passes promptly upon payment confirmation to ensure smooth vehicle exit.
    • Reconcile daily cash and digital collections against DMS billing reports and POS settlement slips, ensuring zero discrepancy.
    • Deposit daily cash collections into the bank or handover to the Accounts department with proper documentation.
    • Coordinate with Service Advisors and Bodyshop Advisors regarding pending payments, split bills, and credit customer accounts.
    • Maintain organized records of invoices, receipts, gate passes, and credit notes for accounting and audit purposes.

    4. Key Performance Indicators (KPIs)

    Reconciliation
    • 100% billing accuracy & daily reconciliation of billing collections with zero financial variance

    5. Key Competencies

    Ability to verify job card details, approvals, invoice lines, taxes, and payment status carefullyKnowledge of basic service and Bodyshop billing, insurance settlement, receipts, gate passes, and credit notesAttention to detail in cash counting, POS settlement, UPI confirmation, bank reference, and DMS reconciliationAbility to identify and escalate billing mismatch, missing approval, payment failure, dispute, or suspected fraudStrong document control, record filing, audit support, and data confidentiality disciplineAbility to explain charges simply while maintaining customer courtesy and financial controlGood coordination with Service Advisors, Bodyshop Advisors, Accounts, and managementCalm, reliable, organized, and ethical conduct during high customer traffic and daily closingPolite, patient, and professional customer communication

    Security Guard

    DepartmentDealership Administration / Security
    Reporting toHR Manager
    Role ImpactPremises Security, Authorized Gate Movement, Asset Protection, Accurate Security Records, and Facility Safety

    Position Overview

    The Security Guard is responsible for controlling authorized access to the dealership, verifying vehicle and material movements, maintaining accurate security records, and protecting people, customer property, dealership assets, and facilities during the assigned shift.

    The role supports orderly customer reception through courteous visitor handling, appointment verification, and accurate gate-in recording. It maintains vigilance across assigned areas through regular patrols, identifies security and safety concerns, and escalates incidents promptly through the approved reporting process.1. 1. Education

    10th / 12th pass with basic security training certification or recognized security experience.

    Training in fire safety, first aid, emergency response, charging-area precautions, visitor management, or CCTV monitoring is desirable.

    2. Experience

    1 to 3 years of experience as a Security Guard in an automotive dealership, commercial complex, or industrial facility.Experience in gate control, visitor management, vehicle and material movement verification, patrol duties, or incident reporting is preferred.

    3. Key Responsibilities

    • Control dealership entry and exit gates, prevent unauthorized access.
    • Verify staff identity, visitor purpose, appointment details (through the available appointment list), and escort requirement before allowing entry.
    • Record details of all incoming & outgoing vehicles (registration number entry & exit time, odometer reading, and initial fuel/battery level) in the gate register or digital system to maintain traceability of such movements
    • Verify each outgoing vehicle against its valid printed (signed & stamped)/digital gate pass (issued) by accounts/cashier before permitting any vehicle to leave the dealership premises.
    • Verify outgoing parts, materials, equipment, scrap against the authorized gate pass/delivery challans.
    • Issue visitor badges, record visitor details, and guide customers politely to the showroom or service reception.
    • Monitor the parking yard, new vehicle stockyard, and workshop perimeter through regular patrolling to prevent theft, vandalism, or damage.
    • Ensure parking driveways, emergency fire exits, and charging bays remain unobstructed by parked cars coordinating team members authorized to drive cars.
    • Maintain vigilance over dealership charging stations and premises, reporting any smoke, sparks, fire hazards, or security risks immediately. Follow the approved emergency procedure, raise the alarm, and notify designated responders without avoidable delay.
    • Ensure smooth shift handovers with updated logbooks covering pending vehicles, visitors, keys, passes, and any active incidents.
    • Coordinate with dealership management and local law enforcement or emergency services when required.
    • Maintain polite and firm conduct. Do not argue, accept unauthorized instructions, or share customer, vehicle, or dealership information.

    4. Key Performance Indicators (KPIs)

    Gate Control & Compliance
    • Accurate and complete entry/exit logging in the security gate register
    • Zero release of vehicles or material without valid authorization.

    5. Key Competencies

    Careful verification of identities, gate passes, vehicle details, materials, and authorizations.Accurate register maintenance, basic digital-record handling, and factual incident reporting.Awareness of dealership zones, restricted areas, parking flow, and emergency access.Alert observation and prompt identification of suspicious activity or safety concerns.Understanding key custody, visitor-badge control, and shift-handover practices.Basic awareness of EV/PHEV charging-area precautions and high-voltage safety boundaries.Calm response to emergencies and adherence to defined escalation procedures.Courteous communication, integrity, confidentiality, punctuality, and firm enforcement of authorized controls.

    General Manager - Service

    DepartmentAfter sales
    Reporting toBusiness Head/CEO
    Role ImpactDealership Performance, Customer Experience & Team Leadership

    Position Overview

    The General Manager – Service is responsible for leading the dealership’s overall Aftersales operations, including Service, Parts, Bodyshop, and Customer Retention. The role drives the Aftersales business plan, profitability, KPI achievement, and customer satisfaction while ensuring operational excellence across all departments.

    The role is also responsible for ensuring adequate manpower, workshop infrastructure, tools, equipment, and compliance with OEM standards and manufacturer requirements, including EV/PHEV service readiness.

    1. Education

    Graduate in Automobile/Mechanical Engineering or related discipline; MBA preferred.15+ years in automotive service/after-sales, with 5+ years in a leadership role.Relevant OEM certifications in service management or dealership operations are an advantage.

    2. Experience

    16–18 years of progressive experience in automotive dealership Aftersales operations, with at least 5–7 years in a department-head or business-head capacity.Demonstrated track record of managing P&L for service, parts, and body shop.Exposure to EV/PHEV service operations, infrastructure planning is highly desirable.

    3. Key Responsibilities

    • Formulate and execute the annual and monthly Aftersales business plan, aligned with JSW and dealership growth objectives.
    • Set department-wise targets (service throughput, parts revenue, body shop revenue, VAS penetration) and conduct regular performance reviews.
    • Own the Aftersales P&L — driving revenue growth, controlling costs, and improving overall profitability and Service absorption.
    • Plan manpower, budgets, tools and infrastructure to support current operations and future business scale-up, including EV/PHEV readiness.
    • Understand Spare Parts operations and monitor at a high level various spare parts inventory levels, availability, ageing and carrying costs in coordination with the Parts Manager.
    • Review and coach department heads (Service Manager, Parts Manager, Body Shop Manager, CRM) on performance against team KPIs.
    • Champion the customer experience agenda — monitoring CSI/NPS trends.
    • Personally review w.r.t. ensuring timely closure and root-cause correction. Also, resolve highly escalated customer complaints
    • Ensure the workshop maintains JSW-mandated EV/PHEV tools, high-voltage safety equipment, and certified technician coverage.
    • Drive cross-functional coordination with Sales to ensure a seamless ownership handover and customer experience.
    • Lead recruitment, training and succession planning for the Aftersales leadership pipeline.
    • Represent the Aftersales function in management reviews, OEM audits, and business planning meetings.

    4. Key Performance Indicators (KPIs)

    Business Performance
    • After sales revenue and profitability (Service, Parts and Bodyshop)
    • Service Absorption Ratio
    • Gross Profit Contribution
    • Revenue per Available Bay
    • Parts Inventory Turnover ratio
    • Parts fill rate/first-pick ratio
    • Service Capacity Utilization
    Customer Experience
    • Customer Satisfaction Index (CSI) / Net Promoter Score (NPS)
    • Complaint resolution turnaround time
    • Customer Retention Rate
    • Service Turnaround Time (TAT)
    • Fixed Right First Time Rate
    People & Governance
    • Department-head performance and target achievement
    • Manpower attrition rate
    • JSW audit compliance score

    5. Key Competencies

    OEM Training ComplianceStrategic business vision, planning and P&L managementStrong functional expertise in Aftersales/dealership service operationsCustomer-centric decision-makingCross-functional leadership and stakeholder managementTeam development, mentorship, coaching, and motivation.Analytical and data-driven problem-solvingUnderstanding of EV/PHEV, safety and infrastructure requirementsInventory and cost control disciplineBudgeting, financial acumen and negotiation skillsOEM standards Audit Score

    CHAPTER 3

    Recruitment and Selection

    "Don't hire just for skills, hire for attitude."
    Objective
    • Implementation of proven recruitment process across the network
    • Manpower with correct skillset is hired
    Benefit for Dealers
    • Plug-and-play recruitment tool
    • Reduced cost of hiring
    • Better quality of manpower hired results in higher retention rates
    • Strong dealership branding and talent pipeline
    Benefit to Customers
    • Transparent and trustworthy business interaction
    • Customer trusts the dealership and the brand

    Principles

    1. 01

      Usage of AI-enabled, blended screening process

    2. 02

      Defined role-based recruitment process

    3. 03

      Well-defined and scientifically proven scoring methodology

    In this chapter, we will look at the standard hiring process to be followed throughout the network.

    3.1.1 Recruitment need

    • Manpower requirement is provided by JSW Motors basis city category and business volumes
    • If the manpower is less than the target, initiate the recruitment process

    3.1.2 Manpower requisition approval

    • Reporting manager sends a request to hire to the HR Manager via email
    • Once HR Manager has received the request, HR Manager fills annexure 3A, discusses and emails the filled form for approval to DP/CEO/GM
    • HR Manager gets the form approved before moving to the next step

    3.1.3 Publish the vacancy

    Internal sourcing

    Internal movement covers promotion, job rotation and transfer between outlets of the same dealership. The HR Manager must explore the following routes before external sourcing:

    SourceCostSpeed of hiringCandidate qualitySuitable for roles
    Internal job posting (IJP)LowFastHighAll roles
    PromotionLowMediumHighAll roles
    Job rotationLowFastVariableAll roles

    How to make an IJP

    • The HR Manager should use 3B. Internal Job Posting (IJP) Template to notify the position internally
    • The HR Manager should display the IJP on notice boards across organisation and share over electronic platforms
    • The HR Manager should reach out to the reporting manager for any recommendation for promotion

    Who can apply for an IJP

    • Completed at least 12 months in the current role
    • Not under a performance improvement plan
    • No live disciplinary case

    *Note that every internal candidate will also have to go through the same interview process as listed in the flowchart above.

    How to apply for an IJP

    • Check the Internal Job postings notice board and electronic platforms
    • Apply for the position by filling up 3C. Internal Job Posting Application Form
    • Email the form to the HR Manager

    Points to note

    • The releasing manager should not intentionally hold/block an internal movement
    • A notice period of up to 30 days is suggested for effective handover of responsibilities
    External sourcing

    External sourcing starts only after an Internal Job Posting has been done. HR Manager should use 3D. Recruitment ad template to advertise the open positions. Use the following table to select the source(s) for external sourcing:

    SourceCostSpeed of hiringCandidate qualitySuitable for roles

    Job fairs and walk-in drivesModerateFastModerateAll roles
    Campus: degree and management collegesModerateSlowModerateEntry level roles
    Internal employees/prospects databaseLowModerateHighAll roles
    *ReferralsLowModerateHighAll roles
    *Employee referral programme
    a. What is the programme

    Under this programme, existing employees can refer suitable candidates and earn a referral bonus for every successful hire.

    b. Who may refer
    • All employees may refer candidates for any open position
    • The HR Manager, HR Executive and anybody on the interview panel may refer but not claim referral bonus for it
    • Referring a family member is permitted post mandatory relationship disclosure using annexure 3E
    c. How it works
    • The referring employee submits the 3E. Employee referral form with the candidate CV to HR
    • The referral bonus is released to referrer after the completion of 30 days of joining of the referred candidate
    • Referral bonus payment is made through payroll and is subject to tax deduction
    • Recommended payout ~INR 2,500 per candidate referred and joined

    3.1.4 Upload the resume

    HR Manager uses the Recruitment Management System (RMS) to screen and interview candidates.

    • Login to RMS portal and select the position and upload CV against that
    • RMS to generate a match score
    • HR Manager reviews match score and sends link to the candidate to upload documents

    3.1.5 Upload documents

    • Screened candidates receive a link to upload the necessary documents
    • The candidate uploads the documents and verifies phone number
    • Once the documents are uploaded, the HR Managers receives documents on RMS
    • The HR Manager must review and approve the documents on RMS to move to the next step

    3.1.6 Conduct psychometric and video-based assessment

    • Upon approval, an online psychometric and video-based AI interaction is triggered to the candidate
    • Post completion of the assessment, a report is generated on RMS
    • HR Manager approves the candidates with more than 70% aggregate score for the next round

    Follow this Interview Panel

    • HR Manager approves candidate to move to interview round 2
    • HR Manager should share annexure 3F with the interviewer(s) along with the candidate CV
    • CEO/GM conducts interview round 2 and enters scores on RMS
    • See annexure 3G for suggested interview questions
    • HR Manager reviews round 2 scores and move the candidates with ≥ 70% aggregate score to interview round 3

    3.1.8 Interview round 3

    • Upon approving the candidate from round 2, a message is triggered to the interviewer as well as the candidate to undergo interview round 3
    • This is the JSW Motors HO approval round and is conducted as per the below table:
    • HR Manager should share annexure where is the annexure 3 F with the interviewer(s) along with the candidate CV
    • See annexure where is the annexure 3 F for suggested interview questionss
    • Evaluation scores are entered online
    • HR Manager initiates the next step of reference and background check
    • All applicants, whether chosen or not, must be informed of the outcome by the HR Manager within seven days of the interview

    3.1.9 Reference and background check

    Reference check and background verification is done in-house by the HR Manager OR through an outsourced partner (refer 3H. Reference check form and 3I. Background verification form).

    What is verified
    CheckDocument and method
    IdentityAadhaar, PAN, passport or voter identity card
    AddressAadhaar, utility bill, rent agreement or bank statement
    Education10th and 12th marksheets, degree certificate and mark sheet for the highest qualification
    Previous employmentAppointment letter from the last employer, last three salary slips, relieving letter and previous one year’s Form 16
    Reference checkMinimum two references
    Police verificationThrough the local police station
    Bank accountCancelled cheque or passbook copy in the employee’s own name
    Medical certificateMedical fitness report to be shared before date of joining
    NOC from previous employerNOC from the current JSW dealership, if applicable

    3.1.10 Movement within the JSW dealer network

    • This applies when the selected candidate is currently employed with another JSW Motors dealership (flagged under “Anti-poaching” in interview round 1)
    • The candidate must obtain a No Objection Certificate (NOC) or clearance certificate from their current dealership before joining the new dealership
    • The HR Manager of the new dealership:
      • a) informs the candidate of the NOC requirement before the offer is released
      • b) issues the offer letter subject to receipt of the NOC (see 3.1.11)
      • c) collects a copy of the NOC before confirming the joining date, and the original on the joining day (see 5.1.5)
    • No joining date is confirmed and no DMS login is created (see 3.1.12) until the NOC is received
    • The current dealership issues the NOC as part of the exit clearance (see 11.1.8)

    3.1.11 Offer letter approval and acceptance

    • The HR Manager must finalise the salary structure as per Chapter 4
    • Prepare the offer letter using annexure 3J
    • Email the offer letter to the reporting manager and the DP for approval
    • Post approval, share the offer letter with the candidate and get their signed acceptance via email
    • For a candidate moving from another JSW Motors dealership, the offer letter states that it is subject to the NOC from the current dealership (see 3.1.10)
    • Upon offer letter acceptance from the candidate, HR Manager sends an acknowledgement message using the below template:
    Dear [Candidate Name], Welcome to [Dealership Name]. Thank you for providing acceptance on the offer letter. We are pleased to welcome you as [Designation Name] for JSW Motors. Your joining date as mentioned in the offer letter is [entre date] at [entre place] at [entre time]. We request you to carry the original copies of the documents submitted for verification. We look forward to welcoming you at [Dealership Name].
    • Keep the reporting manager copied in the acknowledgement email

    3.1.12 Push candidate details to DMS on joining

    • HR Manager accepts the candidate on RMS and pushes the details to DMS
    • For a candidate from another JSW Motors dealership, push the details to DMS only after the NOC is received (see 3.1.10)
    • DMS login is created and shared with the candidate on joining

    3.2 Best Practice

    • Get subscriptions of recruiter versions of job portals as it allows:
      • a faster hiring process by providing advanced candidate filtering options
      • direct candidate messaging
      • CTC/ notice period-based filters
      • automated sourcing tools to identify and contact top talent
    • When hiring next-generation talent:
      • look beyond formal qualifications
      • consider attitude, curiosity, learning ability
      • consider candidates from industries like hospitality, retail, etc. with drive for the automotive sector
    • Maintain a backup pool to:
      • track staff turnover and hire proactively
      • aim to maintain a backup of at least 10% of the frontline staff
      • keep in touch with old employees post their exit
      • keep a list of ‘shortlisted but did not join’ candidates
    • Build a strong social media presence:
      • to attract young and dynamic talent
      • share team photos, employee stories, award ceremonies and appreciation posts
      • present the dealership as a great place to work
    • Interaction via Online Channels:
      • shortlisted candidates get an option to join HR round interview via video calls
      • makes easier to reach candidate and speed up hiring process
    • Employee Referral Scheme:
      • offer non-cash rewards (like movie tickets or family gifts) to top referrers

    CHAPTER 4

    Compensation, Benefits and Incentive Policy

    " Good compensation is not a luxury; it is a prerequisite for sustained growth."
    Objective
    • :
    • To establish a fair, structured and market-aligned compensation structure
    • Attract the right talent, retain strong performers and motivate the entire team
    Benefit to Dealer
    • A structured pay framework reduces salary disputes
    • Performance-linked incentives drive the motivation to achieve dealership business target
    • Reduces attrition, which lowers the cost of hiring and training replacements
    • Statutory compliance protects the dealership from legal risk
    Benefit to Customers
    • Fairly compensated employees deliver a better, more consistent customer experience
    • Well-aligned incentive structures lead to improved employee behaviour and customer relationship

    Principles

    1. 01

      Fixed pay reflecting the role, responsibility and market benchmark

    2. 02

      Variable and incentives tied directly to measurable performance outcomes

    3. 03

      All statutory obligations on compensation and benefits are non-negotiable

    This chapter provides various components of the salary structure along with some benefits given over and above the fixed compensation.

    4.1 Components of Salary

    Total compensation has three components:

    PartWhat it includes
    Fixed payBasic salary, dearness allowance, house rent allowance and any other regular allowance
    Variable payMonthly or quarterly incentive as per policy, linked to performance
    Statutory benefitsProvident Fund, ESIC or medical insurance, gratuity, bonus

    4.3 Changes in Salary

    Salary changes can be considered only in the following situations:

    4.4 Incentive Scheme

    It is a monthly performance reward program for achieving business targets.

    4.5 Best Practice

    • Announce the scheme at the beginning of each quarter, clearly stating monthly targets, eligibility, calculation rules and payout dates. Avoid retrospective changes.
    • Combine business performance with customer satisfaction scores and process adherence.
    • Announce spot incentives on some critical issues like non-moving accessory; sales dead stock items. Always discourage unnecessary selling.
    • Give employees regular visibility of achievement and a monthly statement showing how their incentive was calculated.
    • Adopt a staggered monthly payout cycle (e.g., salary on the 7th, eligible incentives on the 15th, and an optional need-based advance on the 25th) to maintain consistent liquidity and financial well-being for lower-paid employees (technicians and washing team) throughout the month.
    • Upon achieving 100% target, increase incentive progressively, the more one outperforms, the higher their incentive. This way strong performers will stay motivated even after achieving their monthly target.
    • Additional incentive for SA having least outstanding payments.

    CHAPTER 5

    Joining and Confirmation

    "Belonging is not the same thing as feeling like you fit in. Belonging is when you feel valued for everything that makes you stand out."
    Objective
    • :
    • To give every new hire a structured onboarding at the dealership
    • Set expectations during the probation period and confirm employment based on performance
    Benefit to Dealer
    • Well-onboarded employees reach productivity faster
    • Structured joining and confirmation process promotes retention
    • Clear probation criteria prevent disputes during confirmation
    Benefit to Customers
    • Prepared employees handle customer interactions with confidence

    Principles

    1. 01

      A warm, welcoming and professional joining experience

    2. 02

      Confirmation based on performance and behaviour

    The joining process for a new employee helps with their smooth onboarding. The following flowchart highlights the important steps.

    5.1 Joining and Induction Process

    1

    N-3 Send a reminder to the candidate

    HR Manager
    2

    N-2 Remind the reporting manager about the new joiner

    HR Manager
    3

    N Welcome the new joiner

    HR Manager
    4

    N Arrange necessary assets

    HR Manager
    5

    N Complete joining formalities

    N Introduce Dealer Principal, various department heads and the team

    N Explain the induction training

    HR Manager + IDT
    9

    Conduct the 7-day induction training

    HR Manager + IDT

    5.1.1 Send a reminder to the candidate

    • Three days before joining, HR Manager sends a short message to the employee mentioning:
      • dealership address (location map pin)
      • dealership operational timing
      • whom to contact upon arrival
      • any documents to bring along, if applicable
      • any other requirement as per the job role

    5.1.2 Remind the reporting manager about the new joiner

    • Two days before the candidate’s joining:
      • HR Manager sends a reminder email to the reporting manager
      • The reporting manager informs the team about the new joiner

    5.1.3 Welcome the new joiner

    • HR Manager should be available on the joining day or make necessary arrangements in case of unavailability.
    • Welcome the new joiner with a warm gesture like a flower bouquet or chocolates.

    5.1.4 Arrange necessary assets

    • HR Manager must arrange the following assets upon joining:
      • send a request to EDP to create the email and DMS access
      • provide assets as required by the role holder
      • share two sets of uniform
      • issue the identity card
      • add in the dealer communication groups

    5.1.5 Complete joining formalities

    • Complete all the necessary paperwork using annexure 5A with the new joiner like:
      • signing code of conduct
      • documentation of PF, ESIC and nominee details
      • hand over the 5B appointment letter and take the signed copy back
      • collect the original NOC or clearance certificate, if joining from another JSW Motors dealership (see 3.1.10)

    5.1.6 Introduce Dealer Principal, various department heads and the team

    • Arrange an introduction with:
      • reporting manager and the team
      • individual department heads
      • DP or GM

    5.1.7 Introduce Internal Dealer Trainer (IDT) as the buddy

    • On the joining day, introduce the IDT and the new joiner.
    • The IDT will:
      • act as the new joiner’s buddy during the first 3 months
      • give a walkaround of the entire dealership premise

    5.1.8 Conduct the induction

    • Induction is delivered in three parts. The HR department monitors the overall induction, and the IDT conducts the training sessions. On the joining day, the HR Manager and the IDT explain the induction plan to the new joiner.
    • The three parts are:
      • HR Induction – HR Manager, on the joining day
      • General Induction – HR Manager with the IDT, Days 1–2
      • Department Induction – reporting manager with the IDT, Days 2–7
    • The tree below sets out what each part must cover, who delivers it and when.
    • HR Induction – on the joining day, the HR Manager:
      • hands over the welcome letter, joining kit and employee ID card
      • confirms the workstation and required system access
      • completes PF nomination and PF transfer forms (along with the joining paperwork in 5.1.5)
      • explains dealership operational hours, salary date, attendance and leave rules
      • briefs the new joiner on business ethics and the code of conduct
    • General Induction – the HR Manager and IDT take the new joiner through:
      • dealership history, organisation chart, vision, mission and values, quality policy and business objectives
      • working hours, shift timings, breaks, and recording of attendance and late coming
      • pay period, payment mode, group insurance, and ESIC and PF compliance
      • personnel policies – employee classification, probation and confirmation, performance appraisal, discipline and grievance redressal, code of conduct
      • leave types, holidays, leave approvals, leave without pay and leave encashment
    • Department Induction – the reporting manager leads this part with the IDT over Days 2–7. Before it begins, the IDT enrols the new joiner on the LMS, confirms the induction course list and creates the induction training batch in the training management system. The reporting manager then takes the new joiner through:
      • Overview – department goals and objectives and how they link to dealership objectives, department structure and internal working systems
      • Role clarity – roles and responsibilities, reporting structure, coordination with other departments, technical or functional aspects of the job and career progression opportunities
      • Expectation clarity – individual performance criteria (KPIs) aligned to department and dealership goals, and behavioural expectations
      • Training and development – on-the-job training calendar and buddy support from the IDT (see 5.1.7)
      • The reporting manager tailors this part to the role (for example Service Advisor, Technician, Parts, Warranty or Customer Relations), so content and depth will differ by role

    The table below is a suggested day-wise induction sequence for the topics in the tree above. Day 1 is the joining day. The sequence is indicative only; dealerships may adjust the timing to suit their operations, provided every topic in the tree is covered.

    DayThemeTopics to Cover
    Day 1Welcome to JSW MotorsJSW Group & JSW Motors introduction | Dealership introduction | Vision and values |Organisation structure | Introduction to team and department heads | Dealership tour | Buddy introduction |LMS enrolment | Code of conduct, grooming, data privacy and safety
    Day 2Know Your RoleJob description | Roles & responsibilities | Reporting structure | KPIs | Daily work routine | Responsibilities towards customers | Interaction with other departments (will differ from role to role)
    Day 3Know Your ProductCurrent vehicle range and key technologies | Vehicle models | Basic vehicle systems | Service schedules and maintenance requirements | Warranty basics | Genuine parts, approved lubricants and consumables | Common customer queries | Role-appropriate technical and vehicle safety awareness
    Day 4Know Your Customer & After Sales JourneyCustomer expectations | Service appointment and walk-in handling | Vehicle reception and concern capture | Job card creation | Estimation and customer approval | Repair operations and progress updates | Quality checks | Billing and vehicle delivery | Post-service follow-up | Complaint and repeat-repair handling
    Day 5Know Your Systems & ProcessesRole-based DMS and CRM access | LMS | Attendance and leave system | Appointment and customer records | Job card and repair-status updates | Parts requisition and issue records | Warranty documentation | Billing and payment records | Data handling and applicable process standards
    Day 6Learn on the Floor (Role based shadowing)Shadow the buddy or experienced role holder | Observe customer reception, repair workflow and vehicle delivery | Practise role-specific tasks under supervision | Understand coordination between Service Advisors, Technicians, Quality Control, Parts, Warranty and Customer Relations | Reinforce tool handling, housekeeping and safety practices
    Day 7Check Readiness & Set GoalsReview first-week learning | Short role-specific knowledge and safety check | Supervised practical demonstration or customer-interaction role play | Employee questions | Manager and buddy feedback | Confirm performance KPIs | Identify further training and supervision needs | HR records induction completion
    • After induction training completion, the new joiners are nominated for Level 1 or role-based training.

    5.2 Probation and Confirmation Process

    The recommended probation period is three months.

    Basis performance, the management will confirm, extend, or not confirm the employee.

    1

    N-15 Initiate confirmation process

    HR Manager
    2

    N-10 Reporting manager gives confirmation recommendation

    Reporting Manager
    3

    5.2.1 Initiate confirmation process

    • HR Manger initiates the 5C confirmation form and emails it to the reporting manager

    5.2.2 Reporting manager gives confirmation recommendation

    • Reporting manager:
      • fills and sends the confirmation form back to the HR Manager
      • mentions performance, training completed, attendance and conduct
      • gives a clear recommendation

    Either of the three outcomes below can be recommended by the reporting manager:

    OutcomeWhenWhat follows
    ConfirmedPerforming as per expectation, training complete, no conduct problem5D confirmation letter is issued
    ExtendedImproving but not as per expectationsExtended with written reasons and a clear improvement plan
    Not confirmedNot able to do the job even with support, or a conduct problemServices ended as per the notice period in the offer letter

    5.2.3 Inform the employee about the outcome

    • In the discussion, share the outcome with the employee
    • Initiate the next steps according to the outcome – confirmed, extended, or not confirmed

    5.3 Best Practice

    • Create The Right Impression:
      • As the reporting date and time is decided in advance, new joiners should not be left to wait at the reception / lounge
      • HR Manager should personally coordinate and receive them in the designated area with a small pre-welcome act of presenting new joiner with a flower / plant / chocolate pack etc along with a standardized welcome card
    • Welcome Kit and Social Platforms:
      • Giving a welcome hamper containing & dealership co-branded utilities such as diary, pen, bottle, key chain etc is a best practice, encourage the employee to update information of their new role on social media and professional platforms with pictures
      • The dealership can also post a photo about the new joiner on their official social handle and wish them good luck in their new role
    • Publish Organization Announcement:
      • A new joiner announcement e-mailer should be circulated to everyone
      • The email can include the work experience, educational qualifications and department of the new joiner
    • Conduct Periodic Progress Reviews:
      • Conduct structured reviews at agreed intervals during probation rather than waiting until its completion.
    • Buddy Feedback:
      • Daily verbal feedback can be collected by the HR Manager from the IDT on the progress or challenges faced by the new joiner to support them in their new role
    • Use Cross-Functional Feedback:
      • Obtain relevant feedback from the buddy and departments that regularly interact with the employee.
      • Base feedback on observed examples rather than personal opinions or a single customer rating.

    6.2 Introduction to Training Management System

    6.3 Monthly In-house Training Calendar Planning Process

    6.3.1 Planning & scheduling refresher training sessions

    Scheduling Considerations

    • Avoid during planned campaigns and other events.
    • Prioritize participants availability

    Participant Capacity

    • Define maximum capacity based on training mode and space constraints
    • Ensure effective knowledge transfer with appropriate trainer-to-participant ratio

    Session Duration

    • Maximum 2 hours per session
    • Optimal for maintaining engagement and retention while minimizing operational interruption

    Training Modes

    • On-the-Job Training (OJT) – practical, hands-on learning in the work environment
    • Observation-Based Coaching – supervised observation with feedback from trainer or coach
    • Classroom Training – instructor-led, structured learning sessions

    6.4 Non-availability/ Absenteeism for JSW Motors Trainings

    • Participant informs in advance to reporting manager & IDT about non-availability for a training session:
      • Participants unable to attend must inform their Reporting Manager and IDT at least 2 days in advance (except in emergencies).
      • The reason for absenteeism must be documented, and the participant should be scheduled for the next session.
    • Participant does not inform in advance and remains absent without prior intimation:
      • Participant gets a chance to attend next scheduled sessions in case of being absent for genuine reasons.
      • Repeated absence without genuine reason & prior intimation is handled as a breach of discipline and is reported to HR Manager.

    6.5 Failing an Assessment in JSW Motors Trainings

    • For assigned LMS e-learnings, re-take is allowed on the platform.
    • Participants failing the post-test for classroom training must undergo re-training in the next available batch within 30 days to be able to sit for certification assessments.

    6.6 Introduction to Learning Management System (LMS)

    The Learning Management System (LMS) is an app-based digital platform that enables employees to pursue continuous, self-paced learning.

    The key features of the LMS are as follows:

    • Structured and Personalized Learning
      • Role-based learning plans assigned to each participant
      • Clear guidance on the modules to be completed, with real-time visibility of progress
    • Online Assessments & Knowledge Checks
      • Online quizzes, pre- and post-training tests and periodic evaluations
      • Systematic recording of scores, attempts and completion status
    • Digital Knowledge Library
      • A single, searchable repository of product information, SOPs, manuals, FAQs and reference guides
    • Newsletters, Bulletins & Communications
      • Timely circulation of circulars, product updates and official announcements
    • Surveys & Feedback
      • Online feedback forms to capture learners’ views
      • Assessment of training effectiveness
      • Evaluation of content relevance

    The LMS learning path comprises the following five stages:

    6.7 HR & IDT Governance

    The HR Manager & IDT holds the governance for Learning and Development for in-house internal training.

    Governance cadence

    WhatFrequencyWhoHow to Conduct
    Training calendarMonthly, by the 25thIDTNext month module plan and employee nominations
    Training record updateWithin one day of any sessionIDTAttendance, assessment results, certification details

    6.8 Best Practice

    • Internal Dealer Trainer: The HR department, in close consultation with management and the Service Head, should:
      • Select the IDT strictly based on core competencies, including proven technical expertise and OEM certification
      • Position the role as aspirational and respected within the workshop and the wider dealership
      • Discourage nominal appointments or the use of job rotation merely to fill the position
    • One Topic, One Week:
      • A short 10-question test is conducted on a fixed day each week, during a period of low workshop load, through the LMS or another user-friendly platform.
      • Each weekly test is dedicated to a single product, technical system or service process (e.g., EV high-voltage safety, ADAS calibration, job card accuracy, warranty claim procedure)
      • The IDT publishes the leaderboard by the end of the day for the workshop and service front-office teams
    • Expert and Local Speaker Sessions:
      • Each city has accomplished professionals, such as OEM technical specialists, engineering faculty, industry leaders and public officials, recognised for their expertise and achievements
      • Dealerships should invite such speakers to conduct short sessions on technical excellence, workshop safety, leadership and professionalism
    • LMS Dashboard:
      • Use LMS dashboards to monitor training completion for all service roles in real time
      • Track assessment scores and OEM certification status (L1–L3, EV, ADAS) against role requirements

    CHAPTER 7

    Performance Management

    “Where performance is measured, performance improves”
    Purpose
    • structured review process to optimise individual performance
    • alignment with dealership KPIs goals and targets
    • to document and formalise the assessment process
    Benefit to Dealer
    • performance data drives better decisions on promotions, increments and separations
    • underperformance is identified and addressed before it affects business results
    • a performance-driven culture reduces dependency on individual dealerships' informal judgements
    Benefit to Customers
    • accountable employees deliver a more consistent experience
    • teams with clear KPIs resolve queries faster and close transactions more efficiently

    Principles

    1. 01

      goals are set at the start of the year and communicated clearly

    2. 02

      mid-year review and feedback is progressive and goal-oriented

    3. 03

      appraisals are free from bias and backed by data

    Performance management is:

    • career driven – driven by monitoring individual KPIs
    • business driven – governance activities to drive the business

    7.1 Career Driven Performance Management

    The performance of an individual is measured by following these 5 key steps:

    Performance Management Cycle

    Chart 7.1 The Performance Management OR Appraisal Cycle (assuming employee gets inducted in April)

    StepStageWhat happens
    1KPI settingKPIs are set using the SMART model and signed off by the reporting manager and the employee
    2Quarterly reviewOne-on-one progress against the agreed KPIs, recorded on email.
    3Mid-year reviewOne-on-one check on progress, feedback and course correction.
    4Annual appraisalSelf-assessment, manager assessment, rating, grades and review meeting.
    5Increment and promotionRatings and grads are applied to increment and promotion decisions.

    7.2 Performance Management Process

    1

    Define dealership’s annual goals and share with the HR Manager

    CEO
    2

    HR Manager

    7.2.1 Setting KPIs

    Follow the SMART framework while setting KPIs:

    Example:

    Dealership Goal

    Monthly Workshop Throughput = 1,200 repair orders (with 8 Service Advisors) | CSI score of > 95% | Labour revenue of ₹18 lakh and parts revenue of ₹30 lakh per month (assumed average of ₹1,500 labour and ₹2,500 parts per repair order) (this is derived from the Annual Aftersales Business Plan of the dealership)

    Service Advisor KPI

    Handle an average of 450 repair orders per quarter per SA in the financial year | CSI score of 95% for all customers handled in the month | Generate labour revenue of ₹6.75 lakh and parts revenue of ₹11.25 lakh per quarter

    How is it SMART

    Specific – Average 450 repair orders per quarter, with ₹1,500 labour and ₹2,500 parts revenue per repair order | CSI score of 95%

    Measurable – 150 repair orders per month (quarterly repair orders / 3), tracked in the DMS | Labour revenue of ₹2.25 lakh and parts revenue of ₹3.75 lakh per month (monthly repair orders × average labour and parts value per repair order), measured through DMS invoicing | Measurable through the CSI survey and post-service follow-up (PSF) feedback

    Achievable – The goal is realistically achievable

    Relevant – Repair order volume, labour and parts revenue, and CSI score are all relevant for the role of Service Advisor

    Time-bound – Per quarter target, measured every quarter and reviewed at Annual Cycle

    • The set KPIs with their targets should be discussed with employee one-on-one by the reporting manager
    • The agreed KPIs should be emailed to the employee by the reporting manager with HR Manager copied in the email
    • The employee must provide their acceptance on the KPIs email
    • The KPIs must then be added in form 7B by the reporting manager and emailed to the HR Manager

    7.2.2 Quarterly, mid-year and annual reviews

    • 1. HR should remind the reporting managers to conduct the review meetings
    • 2. Reporting manager should schedule a one-on-one review meeting with the employee for all reviews
    • 3. All reviews must be conducted on Business Results dashboard available through DMS to track the KPIs

    Review performance expectations against the set KPIs:

    • 5. During the review meetings, reporting manager must fill form 7B and share it with the HR Manager
    • 6. Document what was agreed on an email with the employee with the HR Manager in cc (sample below) summarizing meeting conclusions about:
      • a. favourable results
      • b. performance issues
      • c. solutions

    Sample email

    From: [Reporting Manager Email Address]

    To: [Employee Email Address]

    Cc: [HR Manager Email Address]

    Subject: Quarterly/Mid-year Performance Review Summary

    Hi [Employee First Name],

    Thank you for sitting down with me today for your quarterly performance review. As discussed, this email summarises our meeting to ensure we are fully aligned moving forward.

    a. Favourable results

    Your hard work reflected in several areas this quarter:

    CSI score of 96% against a target of 95%

    Labour revenue of ₹1,650 per repair order against a target of ₹1,500

    No repeat repairs on the jobs you handled

    b. Performance issues

    You finished the quarter averaging 110 repair orders per month, while our standard is a minimum of 150 repair orders per month.

    c. Solution

    We have committed to the following action plan over the next 30 days:

    Complete a 100% vehicle walk-around with a complete job card at reception for every vehicle

    Attend the IDT’s roleplay sessions on vehicle reception and estimate explanation every week

    We will review your repair orders, labour and parts revenue and job card quality in the DMS every Friday to track your progress and ensure you have the support you need to hit these numbers.

    I have great confidence in your ability to hit these targets, and I am fully committed to helping you succeed. Please reply directly to this email to confirm that this accurately reflects our conversation and your commitment to the plan.

    Best regards,

    [Your Name] Service Manager [Dealership Name]

    7.2.3 The annual appraisal and ratings

    • Using form 7B, calculate the below grade and share it with the employee during their annual review. Note that the rating should not be disclosed to the employee.
    RatingGradeNameIncrement %What it means
    5A+OutstandingTo be decided by the Dealership Management based on business outcomePerformance is well beyond the agreed KPI.
    4AExceeds expectationsTo be decided by the Dealership Management based on business outcomePerformance is consistently better than the agreed KPI.
    3B+Meets expectationsTo be decided by the Dealership Management based on business outcomeKPI is achieved as expected.
    2BNeeds improvementTo be decided by the Dealership Management based on business outcomeFalls short, needs a written plan and support.
    1CUnsatisfactoryTo be decided by the Dealership Management based on business outcomeNot performing as per the agreed KPIs and cannot continue as it is.
    • The manager rates, the Business Head reviews, the Dealer Principal approves while the HR runs the process and keeps it fair
    • A rating of 1 goes to the PIP process below
    • Nobody can be rated 4 or 5 if they have an open disciplinary matter or an integrity concern

    7.2.4 Handling underperformance

    If the reporting manager sees the employee struggling to achieve KPIs before the performance review meetings, initiate mentoring via the following steps:

    Step 1: State the Issue Directly

    "Thank you for sitting down with me. I wanted to review your service targets over the last 90 days. Right now, you are averaging 110 repair orders and ₹1.6 lakh labour revenue per month, while your KPI is 150 repair orders and ₹2.25 lakh labour revenue per month."

    Step 2: Identify the Root Cause

    The root cause may be related to:

    • Knowledge: limited knowledge of products and technical systems, periodic maintenance schedules, warranty and extended-warranty policy, applying proper labour and parts pricing, leading to inaccurate job cards and estimates
    • Skill: does not explain the job requirements clearly to the customer, handle cost objections, or recommend additional jobs and value-added services based on the vehicle walk-around and service history
    • Attitude: low ownership of customer concerns, reluctance to recommend additional jobs, burnout from long hours and peak workshop load, low morale, or personal stress

    Step 3: Co-Create a Corrective Action Plan

    Do not just say "handle more repair orders" or "pick up the pace." Break down into daily, manageable activities like:

    • Scheduling mandatory roleplay sessions on vehicle reception, estimate explanation and upselling of value-added services
    • Setting a baseline of a 100% vehicle walk-around with a complete job card at reception, and every additional job identified shared with the customer for approval
    • Personal mentorship via real-time observation and feedback at the service reception and delivery bays

    Step 4: Establish a Clear Timeline & Follow-Up

    "We are going to review your repair orders, labour and parts revenue and job card quality in the DMS every Friday at 5:00 PM. My goal is to see you hit your daily activity targets, so your repair order and revenue numbers naturally bounce back.”
    • If despite coaching and mentoring, the reviews indicate a consistent decline in performance, the reporting manager must formalise a 4-week Performance Improvement Plan (PIP) using annexure 7C and share with the employee in a one-on-one meeting
    • Reporting manager must conduct a weekly PIP meeting review with the employee in the HR Manager’s presence
    • Note that HR Manager presence is mandatory in all PIP review meetings
    • Conclude the outcome of the PIP post 4 weeks in annexure 7C and if not improved, proceed to termination as per notice period in the offer letter

    7.3 Business Driven Performance Management

    Regular governance activities must be run to drive the business towards achieving its goals, like:

    • daily morning meeting – conducted by SM/GM with all service, body shop (if within the premises) and customer relationship team members
    • mid-monthly meeting – conducted by GM with Service Manager, Bodyshop Manager, CRM
    • monthly meeting - conducted by DP/CEO with GM/Service Manager/HR Manager

    For details on business-driven performance management activities, please see annexure 7D.

    CHAPTER 8

    Career Progression

    " New challenges and opportunities are the two pillars to people growth."
    Purpose
    • Provide employees a visible career path within the dealership
    • Retain strong performers by investing in their growth
    Benefit to Dealer
    • Transparent career paths are one of the strongest retention tools
    • Internal promotions cost less than external hiring and carry lower onboarding risk
    Benefit to Customers
    • Experienced, tenured staff understand the customer base and deliver more personal service
    • Continuity in the team builds long-term customer trust in the dealership

    Principles

    1. 01

      Career ladders defined

    2. 02

      Promotions are criteria-based, not only tenure-based

    This chapter talks about the different career progression path at dealerships.

    8.1 Career Progression Routes

    The table below shows the usual career progression routes in service operations, from entry roles to leadership. Movement to the next step depends on a vacancy and on meeting the criteria in Chart 8.2.

    Note: This table shows movement within the same work area. Lateral movement is also possible and is explained later in this chapter.

    Criteria for moving to the next step

    An employee becomes eligible for the next step only after meeting the minimum experience and the training and certification required for that step. The minimum criteria for each step are given below.

    Step-upMinimum experienceTraining & certificationPerformance & recommendation
    Technician (L1) → Senior Technician (L2)2 years as TechnicianOEM L1 and L2 technical certificationsRating of 3 or more in the last 2 reviews; repeat repairs within norm; Workshop Controller recommendation
    Senior Technician (L2) → Master Technician (L3) / Diagnostic or EV Specialist2 years at L2 (4 years in the workshop)OEM L3 certification; EV high-voltage and/or ADAS specialist certificationFirst-time-right at or above target; Workshop Controller recommendation; Service Manager approval
    Master Technician / Specialist → Workshop Controller / Technical Lead1 year at L3 (5 years in the workshop)Supervisory skills programme; job allocation and bay management trainingTechnician efficiency at or above target; mentoring of junior technicians; Service Manager recommendation
    Denter / Painter → Senior Denter / Senior Painter → Body Shop Supervisor → Body Shop Manager2 years at each step (3 years as Supervisor for Manager)OEM body and paint certification; body shop safety; estimating (for Supervisor); body shop management (for Manager)Rework within norm; Body Shop Supervisor / Body Shop Manager recommendation
    Service Advisor → Senior Service Advisor2 years as Service AdvisorOEM Service Advisor certification; DMS, selling skills, warranty and estimating modulesRevenue per repair order and CSI targets met for 4 consecutive quarters; Service Manager recommendation
    Senior Service Advisor → Workshop Controller2 years as Senior Service AdvisorWorkshop loading and job allocation training; DMS planning; supervisory skills programmeOn-time delivery and throughput targets met; Service Manager recommendation
    Warranty Specialist / Quality Controller / Road Tester → Workshop Controller3 years in the role, with L2 technical certificationOEM warranty and quality certification; workshop loading and job allocation trainingWarranty claim rejections and repeat repairs within norm; Service Manager recommendation
    Workshop Controller / Technical Lead → Service Manager3 years in a supervisory role (7 years in service)Leadership development programme; OEM Service Manager certificationTeam throughput, revenue and CSI targets achieved; Service Head recommendation; panel interview
    Service Manager → Service Head / GM Service3 years as Service Manager (10 years in aftersales)Business management and P&L training; OEM management certificationAftersales P&L targets achieved; GM / CEO recommendation; management panel interview
    CRE Service → Senior CRE Service → CRM Service → CR Head2 years at each stepOEM customer experience certification; complaint management trainingCSI and PSF targets met; CR Head / Service Head recommendation
    Parts Executive → Parts Manager4 years as Parts ExecutiveOEM parts management certification; inventory and DMS trainingFill rate and inventory norms met; Service Head recommendation

    Chart 8.2 Step-up criteria for service roles

    Meeting the minimum criteria makes an employee eligible. The move to the next step is confirmed only after:

    • Senior’s recommendation: a written recommendation from the reporting manager, endorsed by the department head
    • Knowledge: an OEM certification and an internal knowledge test (minimum 80% score) on the products, technical systems and processes of the next role
    • Skill: a practical assessment or on-the-job observation by the IDT and the senior, e.g., live diagnosis, job card and estimate preparation, or bay management
    • Attitude: attendance and discipline record, ownership, teamwork and customer focus, assessed through manager and peer feedback

    All timelines are minimums for guidance. Movement is subject to a vacancy, and exceptional performers may be fast-tracked with the approval of the Service Head and the HR Manager.

    8.2 Promotion Process

    • Promotions are decided at the annual review, with increments, unless a vacancy comes up mid-year
    • Lateral movement is not always a promotion and is covered in later in this chapter
    1

    Follow the IJP process listed in chapter 3

    HR Manager
    2

    Propose the employee for promotion

    Reporting Manager
    3

    Check eligibility

    HR Manager
    4

    Follow assessment process defined in chapter 3

    Reporting Manager with the IDT/ HR Manager
    5

    Take promotion decision upon clearing the assessment

    Reporting Manager with the Business Head
    6

    HR Manager

    Reporting Manager and IDT/ HR Manager

    Eligibility for Promotion

    EligibilityHow it is checked
    Time spent in the current role
    • Minimum 12 months
    • Only confirmed employees should be considered
    Performance
    • Rating of 3 or more in the last annual review. Rating not below 3 in the past two years
    • No pending integrity or disciplinary action
    • Manager feedback captured in the last annual review
    Certification
    • All the required training levels should be completed for the current role
    • Leadership trainings completed before any people-management role

    8.3 Lateral Movement

    • Lateral movement refers to inter-department movement
    • Following employees can opt for lateral movement by applying for an IJP posted by the HR Manager as detailed in chapter 3 section 3.1.3:
      • employees seeking career growth
      • employees seeking a new role more closely aligned with their skillset

    Eligibility to apply for lateral movement is the same as a promotion. Refer Chapter 3.

    If an employee is underperforming in their current role, they can apply for an IJP as mentioned in Chapter 7.

    The table below lists some examples of lateral movement:

    Service Advisor to Warranty SpecialistHas knowledge about job cards, the DMS and customer concerns well; suits detail-oriented employees who can follow OEM warranty procedures
    Master Technician to Quality Controller / Road TesterDiagnostic expertise and an eye for detail help ensure first-time-right repairs and catch issues before delivery
    Master Technician or Senior Service Advisor to Internal Dealer TrainerExperienced employees with an instinct to teach can pass on technical and process skills to new joiners
    Receptionist or CRE Service to Service AdvisorAlready familiar with service customers, appointments and the DMS; a natural step for people-oriented employees who want more responsibility
